Many schools now allow cell phones in classrooms for educational purposes, aiming to help students learn through new, more engaging methods. While completing their assigned tasks, young people also start to consider other productive, creative ways they can use mobile devices in their daily lives.

Teachers see this as a valuable opportunity to guide students on how to use phones responsibly and safely as they grow up. Many educators care deeply about their students’ futures and want to make sure they can progress and succeed in a tech-driven world.

Some teachers still assign traditional paper-based tasks, but many also have students look up recent events or search for class-related information online. This mix of traditional and digital tasks helps students adapt to different learning styles. They even set online exams and quizzes that students complete quickly via phone apps.

When it comes to school policies, some institutions have official rules that permit careful phone use in class, while others set strict regulations that ban mobile devices entirely, no matter the reason. These rules vary widely between different schools and districts.

There are also many government and private programs and organizations that support schools in finding effective teaching methods, helping students pick up new skills that they can apply to their everyday lives.

To sum up, there are countless practical ways to use cell phones as a teaching tool, but schools must always explain the clear purpose behind these activities. It is especially important for schools to teach students how to manage their own phone use responsibly from a young age.

I have often heard teachers ask their entire classes: “What else can you do with your phone besides making calls?” Many students struggle to come up with other useful answers.

Mobile devices have many useful features that can help students grow and improve themselves, as long as they do not waste time on unproductive activities. While it is great that young people spend time in class, using computers, and reading physical books, they should also explore the wider world through new technology.

Many people argue that keeping a positive attitude is the single most important key to success in life, and I completely agree with this idea. When you approach life with an upbeat mindset, you open yourself up to far more opportunities, both in your personal life and your career. This outlook helps you build a brighter future, as you’re more likely to notice and act on chances that come your way, rather than letting them pass by.

A positive attitude also shapes how you interact with others. We all have bad days, and when someone is struggling, offering a kind smile or friendly response can lift their mood and help them work through their problems. This doesn’t just benefit the other person, either—it makes your own day better too. There’s a real sense of satisfaction that comes from knowing you’ve helped someone else, even in a small way, and that positive energy reflects back on your own life. Every day feels easier when you choose to stay positive around others, as seeing someone else smile because of you takes your mind off your own worries for a while.

Your career also benefits hugely from a positive attitude. When you bring good energy to your workplace, you get along better with colleagues and team members. This can lead to more opportunities for promotions or taking on new responsibilities, since people enjoy working with someone who is upbeat and easy to collaborate with. A positive attitude also makes the whole work environment more pleasant for everyone, which in turn makes your own job more enjoyable and helps you perform better. If you treat everyone with kindness and positivity, your workplace will never feel hostile, and that supportive environment will help you achieve even more success.

The same goes for your family life. A positive attitude strengthens your relationships with loved ones, making you feel more supported and content. Family is often the most important support system you have, and maintaining good bonds with them helps you grow into a better person. For example, when my father passed away, my close, positive relationship with the rest of my family helped me cope with the grief and get through that incredibly difficult time. My family supports me every single day, and that strong bond, built on our shared positive attitude, gave me the strength to handle any challenges that came up during that period.

To sum up, I firmly believe that a positive attitude is the key to success in life. It ensures you never feel truly alone, as people are drawn to those who are upbeat and kind. This mindset helps you succeed in every area, whether personal or professional. Remember that good actions bring good rewards, no matter where you go. Even when you’re going through a really tough time, you should never let that change how you treat others—the people around you are not to blame for your problems or bad days. If you are rude or negative to others, you may find they treat you the same way. The best thing you can do is hold onto your positive attitude forever, as that is the surest way to achieve lasting success in all parts of your life.

Thomas Jefferson once shared a brilliant concept about how to achieve any goal we set for ourselves. We all know that finishing tasks that will benefit our future is challenging, but once you complete a task for the first time, working toward that same goal again becomes much less difficult. Still, to reach any goal, everyone has to put in effort and figure out the right steps to make it happen.

When working toward our own aims and goals, we all need to work out how to handle the challenges that pop up. There are often many obstacles to overcome before we reach the target we’ve set, and we all know this process takes a long time. It’s nearly impossible to get there alone, so trying to do it all by yourself will only make the journey harder.

On the other hand, making it a priority to achieve what you truly want, or what you love doing for the rest of your life, is a wonderful choice. Doing so will help you grow into a better person, and even set a positive example for the people around you.

In many rural villages, local schools often organize learning programs for residents, including distance learning options. Community meetings are held to discuss these plans, and nearly everyone gives their approval. A few weeks after the meetings, classes officially begin. Groups of students travel to different areas to teach villagers and check in on their progress. The goal is to make sure villagers can learn all the skills they need for daily life.

I strongly believe that students benefit greatly from being able to attend classes from their own homes, especially those living in rural villages.

My first reason is that in many villages, barely anyone used to attend school. Most residents spent all their time doing hard physical labor. One day, a group of people visited these villages and decided to start teaching the locals. They launched classes soon after. At first, some villagers thought the idea was ridiculous, but once everyone started learning, they realized how valuable education was for the whole community. These classes, often held online or via video, teach practical skills: how to plant and maintain home gardens, how to grow and develop, how to grow crops successfully, and how to reduce the amount of hard physical work they have to do. The first big challenge was changing how people viewed education.

My second reason is that people who never study will run into many avoidable problems later in life, which is exactly why education is so necessary. Some villagers still believe that studying is a bad thing that holds people back in life. To address this, educators teach them several key lessons: first, girls should not be married before they turn 18. Second, they learn about ways to plan their families and control birth rates. Third, they are taught that everyone deserves a bright future. Fourth, both boys and girls have an equal right to education.

My third reason is that good education is a basic need for people all over the world, especially for future generations. People who never get the chance to study often struggle to communicate with others outside their community. I stand by this point because education is essential for everyone. Nowadays, more villagers are attending school themselves, and they are also sending their children to classes. The students who run these programs help villagers with every part of their daily lives, not just schoolwork.

To sum up, people need access to education every single day, whether it is for a few seconds, a minute, or a full year. Without education, communities are more likely to stay trapped in poverty. I fully support the decision made by local schools to bring these learning programs to villages, as it has made a huge difference. Learning never truly ends—we pick up new things every day, and this process continues throughout our lives, even until the day we die. We also need to keep supporting the students who teach these classes and make sure villagers have all the resources they need to keep learning.

I believe older children should not be grouped with younger kids, as they often set poor examples, behave inappropriately around little ones, and show a lack of respect for them.

I strongly think these age groups should not mix. When an older child acts out or tries something risky, younger kids are likely to copy them without understanding the danger. This can lead to serious accidents. For example, my brother and his friend were practicing skateboard tricks once, and I tried to copy a move I wasn’t ready for. I fell hard and ended up breaking my arm.

Another issue is that older kids may experiment with drugs or smoking, which is incredibly harmful to younger children nearby. Secondhand smoke can damage little kids’ lungs, and long-term exposure might even lead to cancer or death. A friend of mine, Generic_Name, had a brother who would smoke right next to us. We warned him that smoking could kill both him and us, but he refused to listen.

Older children should treat younger kids and everyone else with respect. When they act politely, younger kids learn to do the same. But if an older child is rude, younger children will copy that bad behavior. For instance, a friend’s brother was constantly disrespectful to our group, so we stopped being polite to him in return.

All these reasons are why I think older kids should not spend time around younger children. They often lack respect, set poor examples, and don’t act appropriately with little ones. If older kids were more responsible and polite, mixing the age groups might be fine, but as things stand, it’s a bad idea.

Do students gain advantages from being allowed to take classes from home? I believe learners can gain a lot from this setup, as long as they complete their coursework remotely via video calls or online platforms. This arrangement gives students more chances to focus on their studies and even fit in part-time work, since they no longer have to waste time walking or taking the bus to campus. Learning from home also tends to be more productive, as the environment is usually quieter than a busy school classroom where people often chat about unrelated topics instead of paying attention to the lesson. On top of that, remote classes let students pick when they start their lessons, which is helpful for those who have part-time jobs. They also do not have to travel to school on cold, unpleasant days. While some might argue this makes students more responsible, that really depends on the person – but there are still plenty of clear benefits to this system regardless of a student’s habits. Many students find working from home far less stressful. They can take short breaks when they need to, grab a snack while they study, and put more of their mental energy into learning instead of dealing with school-day distractions. Overall, I think remote learning via online tools or video conferences is the best way for students to learn. That said, it does depend on the individual – some students get lazy when they are not in a physical classroom. Parents can also keep an eye on their children’s progress this way, checking if they are completing assignments well or falling behind. For me personally, doing homework is much easier when I am at home, too. To sum up, even with the small risk of some students slacking off, allowing learners to attend classes from home brings far more benefits than drawbacks.

When I first arrived in the United States, I could not speak any English. Every time I went out to play or headed to school, the people around me would use simple examples to show me what to do or where to go. If I wanted to play soccer or visit the playground, I would point out the window or sketch a quick picture of what I meant. I tried to find other ways to communicate my needs, but before I learned English, giving examples was the only option available to me.

There is a common claim that examples are not just the main way to influence others—they are the only way, because they are the only method that helps people understand what you are trying to say. Everyone uses examples to help each other make sense of new ideas. However, some people disagree, arguing that there are many other tools to influence others. For example, Google Translate, Google search, YouTube, and countless other apps all help people share information and influence each other.

I agree that examples are not just the primary way to influence others; they are the only way. Examples are used everywhere, in almost every situation, even when you are trying to speak to someone who speaks a completely different language. Children look up to adults and copy their actions, so adults constantly set examples for kids. This applies to everything, including parenting: if a parent wants their child to behave well, they have to act as good examples for their children, or show their child clear examples of how to act properly. How we behave is incredibly important, because it shows others how to act and sets a standard for appropriate behavior in specific places. For instance, if a child goes to a library and sees two adults being loud and fooling around, they will copy that behavior. They assume the adults know how to act in a library, so their loud actions must be acceptable.

Still, others argue that examples are not the only way to influence others, because technology has created many other options for us to connect and influence each other. For example, if I travel to another country, I do not need to draw a picture of a museum or point at things to get directions. I can type what I need into Google Translate, show it to a local, and get the information I need. Students who are still learning English can use dictionaries or Google to help them understand their lessons.

Aesop, the ancient Greek storyteller, once noted that no act of kindness is ever wasted, no matter how small it might be.

Even tiny gestures of kindness can have a real impact on other people. This is because doing something good, completing meaningful tasks, or helping someone in need all create positive change.

First, simple kind acts like giving food to a hungry person can make a big difference. You are doing something important that many others might not bother to do, so your small gesture has a real effect on that person.

Second, small acts of kindness also matter when you do something important, like taking care of something that needs attention.

Third, helping someone else, like saving a person’s important work when they cannot do it themselves, has a clear impact. Their work matters to them, so your help makes a significant difference to their day.

It does not matter how small or large a kind act is. What is truly important is that you are taking action to help others, do good for the people around you, and make their lives a little better.

Adopting homeless teenagers is incredibly beneficial for young people, as it can steer them away from risky behavior, including breaking the law. This process gives teens a stable home, access to education, and a far better quality of life overall. What these young people need most is supportive parents who will help them with every aspect of their lives, since parental figures are some of the most important people we have. Many teens living on the streets wonder why they cannot have a better home or life, and it is heartbreaking for them to see other young people enjoying all the good things that come with having a family. Street kids often do not realize that their lack of education puts them at risk of getting into trouble, as they act without thinking due to the harsh realities of living on the streets and breaking laws. There are many reasons why teens end up in this situation: they missed out on education at a young age and never got to develop their learning skills. Curfews also help keep teenagers out of trouble and reduce violations of local street rules, but adopting homeless teens addresses the root of the problem. This would cut down on the many incidents caused by their reckless behavior that lands them in trouble, as what these teens really need is consistent support from someone who wants to help them. Many street teens do not even realize they could go back to school or seek help to turn their lives around.

Once a homeless teenager is adopted, they can pursue their dreams and share their thoughts freely after moving into their new family’s home. For example, adopted teens often work hard in their studies, reach goals they never thought possible, and stay out of legal trouble.

Have you ever thought about whether picking a career early in life is a smart move? I strongly believe it is, especially since many communities expect young people to decide on a career path by the time they start high school.

High schools structure their classes to guide students toward particular career paths. One major benefit of choosing a career early is that students start high school with a clear sense of what they want to do after graduating, which keeps them motivated. Another key point is that early career choices help students pick the right high school diploma. Most schools offer two main options: an advanced diploma, which requires passing 9 SOL exams and completing all required classes, and a standard diploma, which only needs 6 SOL passes and all mandatory courses. When students start high school, their counselors work with them to pick the diploma that matches their chosen career and future goals.

During 9th and 10th grade, students take basic, required classes that help them build core knowledge and get early experience tied to their career goals. This makes it easier and faster to progress, as they already understand their objectives and are prepared for the final two years of high school.

Even if a student wants to change their career choice later, teachers and counselors are always there to help. They can explain the benefits of different career paths, including how much money a certain job can earn, to help students make informed choices. This support ensures students can succeed and build a stable life with their chosen career after graduating high school.

The final two years of high school, 11th and 12th grade, include more challenging classes that students must pass to graduate. 11th grade is often the toughest, as students need to pass two key classes to move on to 12th grade. In 12th grade, students only take the classes their counselor recommends, which are matched to the diploma they chose (advanced or standard) and the career they plan to pursue after graduation.

To sum up, choosing a career at a young age is a fantastic idea. It gets students thinking early about their future goals, what career suits them, and how that path will benefit them long-term. High schools prepare students for life after graduation, whether that means going to a four-year college to improve their quality of life, or going to NOVA to get ready for the career they have chosen. Students who start early already have the knowledge to pick a career they will succeed in, and can turn their future dreams into reality.

There are countless career options available for young people to build successful lives. That is why I believe students should start thinking about their career when they enter high school, where teachers and counselors will do their best to help them pick a path they are truly interested in. This early planning helps students succeed in college, build a better life for themselves and their families, and achieve their long-term goals. All of this makes choosing a career at a young age an excellent choice.

Certain school districts now run programs that let high school students finish their studies and graduate in three years, rather than the standard four. Many of these students, and other high schoolers across the country, are immigrants who moved here from other nations with different languages and cultural backgrounds. This makes earning a high school diploma far more difficult than it is for native English speakers. When you can’t speak the language, you can’t follow lessons, complete assignments, or pass exams, which means some students need to stay all four years just to keep up. But putting in effort to pass your classes is key to building a good future for yourself.

I am one of these immigrant students. I moved to this country three years ago, and at the time I spoke almost no English. Getting through my classes was incredibly tough at first, but I kept pushing because I want to build a better life for my mom and little brother. There are so many more opportunities here than in my home country, and I want to graduate to give my family a chance at a brighter future. Recently, I passed the Algebra 1 SOL exam, and I was so relieved and happy when I got my score. Even though my family and I still face a lot of challenges, passing that test felt like a big step forward.

Some students even take a break from school to work for a year or more before going to college. They do this to earn money and support their families, while still working toward their long-term goal of building a stable future for the people they love.

Do curfews keep teenagers out of trouble?

Many people argue that setting strict time limits for young people unfairly intrudes on their personal freedom. While the official goal of these rules is to keep teens safe, plenty of young people feel that curfews are an unwanted interference in their daily lives. Adults want teenagers to stay out of harm's way, but most teens dislike being told exactly what they can and cannot do.

Most curfews ban anyone under 18 from being on the streets after 10pm on weekdays, and midnight on weekends. Teens who are out past these hours are technically breaking the law. Even though curfew supporters claim they do not want to disrupt young people's lives, these rules still affect how teens can spend their time. Many people resent being ordered around by these policies, and there is little evidence that curfews are actually effective. If they really worked as intended, all teen-related trouble would already be eliminated.

In my view, it is unfair for authorities to impose these rules on others. Curfew officials might believe they are doing the right thing, but their efforts have not solved the underlying issues. I do not think these curfews are necessary. Some people may approve of them, but they are definitely not popular with everyone.

I’m a student at Generic_School, and I work four days a week once classes end each day. My shifts are full days, but they always go by quickly. After I finish high school, I plan to attend university for four years. My long-term goal is to open my own business, hire staff, earn a good income, and eventually expand my company to open branches in other locations.

For high school students who work four days a week, balancing school and a job takes effort, but it’s a necessary part of planning for their future. They need support to manage their daily lives, and often ask friends, family, or teachers for time management advice to handle both schoolwork and shifts each day. This helps them graduate on time and find a good job later. Earning money is important for their future: they hope to buy a house, own a car, and live a happy, comfortable life.

I believe both school and part-time work during your studies are valuable for your future. School teaches you the skills you need to finish high school and get into university, while working after classes helps you earn money to support yourself. If you want to become a business owner, which can bring in a high income, you still need to learn how to run a company first. Opening your own business means hiring employees, making a profit, and expanding to new locations, which lets you achieve goals like owning a home, buying a car, and living a happy life. Beyond personal goals, opening more schools in other areas can help people who struggle financially find work, reduce conflict and war between countries, and make the world better for people who lack basic needs like food and housing.

I still stand by the idea that school and work during your studies set you up for a good future, by helping you finish high school and move on to university. Even though students who work during school don’t earn much at first, so they can’t afford a house or a car right away. After graduating high school, they need to pay for university classes, housing, and food. Once they finish their degree, they can get a full-time job and earn enough to meet their future goals: a home, a car, and a happy life. The time management skills they learn from working four days a week also help them support others. Finishing high school, going to university, and working part-time all help you build a secure financial future, and if you want to be a business owner, you need to learn how businesses operate first, often by learning from experienced owners who can mentor you. Finally, all schools need proper funding to help students study well, especially in subjects like math and science, so they can finish university, get good jobs, earn a living, and live a good life.

Dear Principal,

I am writing to express my full support for your proposal to change the school lunch menu. This adjustment would be beneficial for both the school and the student body, as it gives us a chance to try out healthier, more varied meal options.

Many students would welcome this change, since we have been served the exact same dishes every day since the start of the school year, and a bit of variety would be a refreshing change. Of course, some students might not like the idea, as they already have favorite meals on the current menu that they do not want to give up. That said, most students would likely be happy to switch to better, more appealing food choices.

This plan is worth considering for another reason, too: right now, a lot of students skip school lunches entirely. Some leave campus to buy food at local restaurants, while others bring homemade packed lunches instead of eating the meals provided by the school.

In my opinion, it is far better to try something new and see how students react to the menu change in the future, rather than serving the same food year after year. There is always a risk that the new menu could be worse, and students might dislike the updates. But it could also be a great success, encouraging far more students to eat school lunches regularly.

I believe after-school homework clubs are a great resource for schools. For one, students can work at their own pace to fully grasp the material they’re assigned, rather than rushing through tasks. They can get all their homework done during the club session too, so they don’t have to worry about completing assignments later at home. Teachers who are passionate about their subject and genuinely want their students to earn good grades across all classes can offer far more one-on-one support in this setting than they could during regular class time.

It’s common for some students to struggle with assigned work or fall behind the rest of the class. Homework club gives these learners a chance to catch up, and even finish entire units of work ahead of schedule if they put in the effort. Students who are already caught up can also use the time to support peers who are struggling, or assist those who are unable to attend the club in person.

These clubs also benefit teachers who truly care about education. Educators who enjoy going beyond basic lessons to help students stuck on a problem, and who have free time after school—for example, those without young children of their own or no other commitments—often find running homework clubs very rewarding. While some teachers only show up to deliver lessons, collect their paycheck, and leave, others are deeply committed to their work. They like guiding students through mistakes and giving helpful corrections to help them improve.

Another key advantage is that students with packed schedules can get their work done. Many children have busy after-school routines, with activities like soccer, baseball, or basketball taking up their free time. If schools provide after-school buses, these students can attend homework club to complete assignments they would otherwise have no time for. This is especially important for children who need to care for younger siblings because their parents work long hours, or for families where a parent is sick and needs constant care. Without access to a homework club, these students would have no time or energy left to do schoolwork at home.

Overall, I think after-school homework clubs are a positive addition to any school. They give students a chance to finish work they might otherwise struggle to complete, or get extra help understanding tricky material. If there are 10 or 20 minutes left at the end of a session once everyone has finished their assigned work, staff can even use that time to introduce students to new, interesting topics.

Most traditional high schools require four years of study, spanning grades 9 to 12, for students to earn their diploma. That said, a number of schools now run fast-track programs that let learners finish their high school education in just three years. These fast-track options typically work in one of three ways: attending summer school classes, taking evening courses, or skipping all elective classes to focus only on required subjects.

My first reason for supporting three-year high school programs is that all high school students are teenagers, and they need time to handle personal responsibilities. Finishing school a year early gives them the chance to get their driver’s license, set up insurance, and take care of other key tasks they will need as they grow up.

My second reason is that all high school students are teenagers, some of whom work to save for college. Graduating in three years lets them work a full extra year to put money aside for college costs.

My third reason is that students who take part in these three-year programs have far more options available to them. They can secure spots at good colleges, choose to live close to their family, and find well-paying jobs sooner than their peers.

I think these programs are a great option for students who want to go to college.

I fully agree that each person is responsible for shaping their own character through the choices they make. For me, this means three key things: first, I will choose the path I follow for my future career; second, I will decide to be someone who interacts openly with others; and third, I will make sure my character prioritizes taking care of my physical health.

When it comes to my future, I will decide what kind of person I become. My parents want me to be a doctor, and push me to follow that path. But I disagree—I have dreamed of being a pilot for years. I will choose between their wish and my dream, picking what works best for me. That choice will shape my character.

I genuinely enjoy being around others, so I will choose to be someone who seeks out social interactions. Spending time with people in my life helps me work out how to build the character I want. Being social means I can form more friendships, and the time I spend with these friends lets me pick up new skills and learn from their unique experiences, all of which contribute to shaping who I am.

Finally, my character will prioritize staying healthy. Good health is very important to me, and my health depends on the choices I make about my character. Eating nutritious food keeps my mind clear, helping me make better decisions. If my health declines, I won’t have the energy to stick to the character I’ve chosen. That is why health is essential to maintaining control over who I become.

To sum up, I believe each person’s character comes from their own choices. I plan to be a pilot, and will decide whether to follow that dream or my parents’ wish for me to be a doctor. Spending time with others helps me build my character, and poor health would stop me from living it out. All these choices are mine to make, and will shape who I become.

I disagree with the statement that a positive attitude can solve every problem life throws at you. There are countless struggles that simply cannot be fixed just by staying optimistic.

For instance, think about a person who arrives in the United States alone, with no one to help them. If they are undocumented, they miss out on many benefits that citizens get from birth. They may not speak the language, have to avoid police, and cannot find good jobs because of their legal status. It is impossible to just “be positive” when you are dealing with all of these practical struggles.

Another case is when someone close to you in your family gets very sick or passes away, but you are in a different country and cannot travel to see them. You cannot just stay positive through that kind of pain. This is one of the main reasons I believe positivity is not the answer to all of life’s struggles.

Immigrants also face constant discrimination. Many locals assume moving to the US was easy, and do not realize the dangers people go through to get here. They may judge you based on your skin color, or assume you only came to make money and return home, when many are here to build a new life. Most people do not understand this, and treat immigrants terribly. It is hard to keep a positive attitude when you are treated unfairly day after day.

Of course, there are plenty of things to feel positive about: supportive family, friends, a partner, a good job, or graduating high school are all reasons to be happy. But even with these good things, there are times when you just cannot stay upbeat. For example, if you are struggling financially, friends may say they cannot help because they have no money—but you know they are lying. Realizing they are pretending makes you feel like they are mocking your struggle, which definitely does not make you feel positive.

My main point is that even if you try your hardest to stay positive, bad things will still happen that drag you down. For immigrants, not being able to see your family back home is one of those things that can make you feel negative, no matter how much you try to look on the bright side. That is exactly why I disagree that a positive attitude can solve all of life’s problems.

I firmly agree that making an effort to learn topics or skills beyond what you have already mastered is extremely valuable. Trying to go past your current abilities is always worthwhile—if you never take that first step, you will never discover what new things you could learn.

There are two main benefits to this approach. First, it lets you gain far more knowledge and learn new facts. When you push past what you already know, you pick up all kinds of new information. For instance, you might learn how to explore unfamiliar parts of the world, figure out how cars are built from scratch, or even understand the steps needed to set up factories. This extra effort also helps you gain specialist knowledge in all sorts of areas. You could learn how to teach science more effectively, pick up facts about outer space, or even find out how to turn a regular car into a robot.

Beyond just gaining facts, pushing your boundaries also makes you more open-minded. For example, you might learn how to write a clear essay, pick up skills to coach a team, or even gain the experience needed to serve as a member of congress.

To sum up, putting in hard work to learn beyond what you already know is always the better choice. It allows you to pick up more knowledge and become more open-minded, both of which are impossible if you only stick to what you have already mastered.

Modern classroom technology, especially computers, has become a valuable tool for schools. They make it easier to carry out more assessments, and there is a wide range of software available to help students learn how to create presentations or complete projects.

For example, Microsoft Office programs let students master Word to write formal letters, or PowerPoint to put together presentations that would work well in professional business settings.

Computers also make research far simpler. I can look up details for my school projects or history assignments, since the internet holds a huge amount of information on almost any topic. Practicing typing on computers also helps boost my accuracy and speed. I pick up new vocabulary too, which makes putting together projects much easier and saves me a lot of time.

Digital devices are also good forthe environment. We don’t need to cut down as many trees to make paper, which protects natural ecosystems. Instead, we can plant more trees in local parks to create nicer green spaces that everyone can enjoy. I can even bring my laptop or tablet to the park to finish my homework outside.

Staying true to who you are means being honest with both yourself and the people around you. For instance, when you’re spending time with a group of friends, don’t try to act like a completely different person. Eventually, people will see through the act, and you might end up getting teased for pretending to be someone you’re not. It’s far better to let people like the real you, rather than putting on a fake persona that forces you to lie to yourself and everyone else.

Ralph Waldo Emerson, a well-known writer, once said that “to be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.” I fully agree with this idea, though not everyone feels the same way. Far too many people on this planet struggle to stay true to themselves, choosing instead to copy others rather than embrace who they really are.

A big reason so many people find it hard to be authentic is pressure from society. Society often pushes people to act like someone they’re not, rather than encouraging them to stay true to their own identity.

Nowadays, some people even think being authentic is boring, while pretending to be someone else seems cool. But there are clear downsides to faking who you are. You might lie to people until they eventually discover your true personality, and if they don’t like the real you, your feelings will get hurt. You might even end up without friends and feeling defeated. But you can always turn things around by choosing to be yourself again. Over time, people will notice the change, and they’ll want to build genuine connections with you.

Being yourself also makes for much healthier relationships than pretending to be someone else. The main reason for this is simple: you don’t want to spend the entire time lying to the person you’re close to. That kind of dishonesty always leads to conflict down the line. If you have been faking it, though, it’s never too late to talk things through and tell the truth.

Choosing to be authentic can have a huge impact on your daily life. This effect can be positive or negative, depending entirely on the choices you make. That’s why it’s so important to stay true to yourself at all times, no matter what the cost. Above all, take pride in who you are, exactly as you are.

There’s nothing more rewarding than finally reaching a goal you’ve worked toward for years, no matter how long the journey takes.

Staying true to who you are is especially hard in a world that shifts constantly, and where plenty of people will judge the life choices you make. It’s easy to overthink every comment others make about your plans, but if you want to climb higher than your current position, you have to make firm decisions that push you toward the big accomplishments you’re chasing, even if they’re unpopular.

I fully agree with the idea that staying authentic is the ultimate achievement. Time moves forward whether we act or not, and the more effort you put in, the more you get out of life — something many people fail to realize. If you want to achieve meaningful things, you have to put in the work. Take LeBron James as an example: how do you think he reached the top of his field? He set clear goals, took small steps toward them, relied on support from his family, and used every resource available to him. All the tools you need to succeed are already within reach; you just have to go out and claim them.

That famous quote about staying yourself when the world tries to turn you into someone else? I don’t think it means the world is forcing you to change. You’re the one in control of your own life. Sure, you’ll face setbacks and make mistakes along the way, but those are exactly how you learn to reach what you want. If you cut corners early on, you’ll end up with low-quality, short-lived results. But if you put in hard work from the start, things will feel much easier by the end, and you’ll be grateful you put in the effort.

What counts as a great accomplishment looks different for everyone. Every person has their own path and potential — whether you want to be a teacher, a parent, a friend, or something else entirely, you have the power to make it happen. The people around you, like family, teachers, or friends, can only point you toward opportunities. They won’t open doors for you, and neither will your parents or mentors. You’re the only one who can choose to turn the handle and step through to reach your goals.

I’m proof of this myself. I used to hate school so much that there were times I refused to even go. Back then, I had an F in my English 10 class, until one day my teacher pulled me aside for a single conversation. I spent a lot of time reflecting on what she said, and by the end of the term, I’d pulled my grade up to a B. I never thought I was capable of that, but I just focused on doing what I needed to do. Like I said before, people can only show you where the opportunities are — you have to go after them yourself.

That quote about staying yourself being the greatest accomplishment? It’s absolutely true. Pull yourself together, and don’t be afraid to ask for help from people you trust — good people will always want to support you. Staying silent about what you need won’t get you anywhere. Asking for help isn’t a sign of weakness; it makes you stronger. That’s exactly what we all need: the strength to chase our goals and cross the finish line.

Research shows that 85% of people only stick to tasks they have already mastered, rather than trying new activities. This is a major problem. Many people today think sticking to what they already know is the best choice, but repeating old habits stops them from growing. These familiar routines will not benefit them later in life.

I completely disagree with this habit of repeating the same actions over and over. First, trying new things can improve your future prospects. Second, you should never feel nervous about doing things in a different way. Third, you should not always act exactly like your usual self, because if you never try new experiences, you will never truly understand the world around you or even learn who you really are.

Trying new things can shape your future for the better. For instance, my sister once fell into the same trap of wasting time on repetitive habits. My mom sat her down one day and warned her that she would never reach her goals if she did not start planning for her future. After that talk, my sister stopped repeating the same old routines, worked hard, and is now a successful doctor.

You should also never feel afraid to take a different path. My dad, for example, was once terrified to start his own business. He worried that the work would be completely unfamiliar and too hard to handle. I told him that if he never tried new approaches, our whole family would never make progress. He finally took the leap, and now his company is doing very well. The experience has helped him a lot, as he put in hard work to make it succeed.

Finally, always being your "true self" is not always good advice. If you only act exactly how you always have, you will never learn about the world or discover new parts of your own personality. My mom used to tell me to always be myself, but I explained to her that this is not a great rule. If you only stick to what feels natural, you will never achieve the things you want in life. Our usual selves tend to prefer easy, simple tasks, and we rarely push ourselves to work hard enough to reach our biggest goals.

To sum up, I believe it is wrong for people to keep doing only what they have already mastered, as this stops them from growing into the person they want to be. We all need to start thinking seriously about our futures, try new things, and avoid the trap of only sticking to our usual habits.

There are two opposing views on decision-making: some believe individuals should make their own choices, while others argue against this. I believe everyone should make their own decisions. Our lives belong to us, so no one else can pick our path. Everyone has the right to freedom, and we can work towards whatever future we want. No one wants their life compared to someone else’s, and we all need to be in control of our own lives.

If we study hard and work diligently, we can achieve the goals we set. Families play a big role here. Parents should encourage children to study and plan for their future. Without family support, it’s harder for young people to make choices or grow. We should also care for our families, support them in return, and build good lives together.

Each person must stand by their own choices and be open to others, while listening to family advice. Family members want the best for us and never trick us. If we lack family support, we have to rely on ourselves. For those wanting a bright future, good job, or recognition, a support system helps. But without backers, you must be your own biggest supporter.

Listen to others’ ideas as you plan your future, but no one else can make your decisions. Most want to be driven “seekers” in life, as focused people achieve goals more easily. Patience also matters—patient people grow steadily and reach targets faster. To sum up, being determined, bold, and patient helps you make your own choices, reach goals, and build a happy future.

Ifyou only ever attempt tasks you’ve already fully mastered, you’ll never make progress or grow as a person. You’ll stay stuck acting like a small child who never matures. Do you really go through life only doing things you already know how to do perfectly? Even when you’re little, you can’t keep running to your parents saying, "Mom, Dad, I don’t know how to do this, I don’t know how to do that," and expect them to handle every single task for you. If you never make an effort to try on your own, you’ll never develop or grow up.

You’re not a baby anymore, so you need to start handling tasks on your own. When I was younger, I didn’t really get what it meant to do things for myself. My older sister would constantly ask me to help her with small chores: washing dishes, hanging up wet laundry, little things like that. She never lifted a finger to do even the simplest of these tasks herself.

One time, my grandmother walked in and saw me hanging up clothes. She immediately told me to stop, saying it was too dangerous and I should come over to her. She asked who had told me to do the laundry, and I quietly said it was Generic_Name. My grandma got really angry then, scolding my sister: "Why are you so lazy? You’re perfectly capable of doing all these things yourself." My sister started crying loudly after that.

Everyone has a capable, smart brain. I used to be extremely lazy myself. Whenever I came across something I didn’t know how to do, I wouldn’t even bother trying to work it out—I’d just go ask my parents or my sister to handle it for me. If you never attempt tasks that go beyond what you’ve already mastered, you’ll never grow into a successful adult.

Most people have at least a small amount of mastery in different areas. If you pick up even a little bit of skill in lots of different things, you’re already halfway to success.

Learning from other people’s past experiences is really important. There is always a chance that you will face the exact same situation as someone else one day. If that happens, you will already be prepared, instead of feeling scared about what might happen to you or the people around you. That’s why, if you meet someone who has already dealt with the same issue you are facing, it makes sense to ask them what happened, how they fixed it, and whether extra help is available if needed.

Another helpful step is to talk to older family members, like your grandma, about problems they have faced in the past. Ask what solutions they chose, and why they picked those options. This way, if you ever run into the same issue, you will know what actions to avoid, and what choices are open to you. It is key to ask these questions before the problem affects you or people you care about.

If you don’t ask about others’ experiences before a problem hits you or your family, you won’t be able to do much when it actually occurs. But if you prepare ahead of time, you will know how to handle the issue yourself, or support the people you care about and love. These are some of the best ways to tackle the kinds of problems you might face in life.

You can’t help other people if you stay silent. Instead, you should ask if you can do anything to support someone who is going through a hard time, and find out what kind of problem they are facing. Some issues can be very serious, even life-threatening, so it is important not to ignore them.

Some people end up without any family because they refuse to let others help them with their struggles. They try to solve every problem on their own, but the truth is, everyone needs help sometimes. You cannot get through life without support — this is something you have to accept. If you are in serious trouble and refuse help, you could end up in a life-threatening situation.

When people need guidance, they often reach out to more than one person for input. This usually happens because they’re facing a tough situation—whether it’s personal trouble, low mood, or even a big happy event like a celebration—and feel like they can’t make decisions on their own. They might feel panicked, unsure of what steps to take, so they turn to others for help. While getting multiple perspectives can be useful, it often backfires: too many conflicting opinions leave people confused, unable to pick a single piece of advice that works for them. In my view, it’s perfectly fine to ask others for their thoughts, but you have to use your own mind too. You can’t function well without your own judgment. When someone shares an opinion, take time to think it over: what are they suggesting? Does it fit your needs? Could following their advice lead to trouble later? If you’re still unsure, you might run the idea by a close friend or family member you trust—if they agree, you might feel more confident moving forward.

You don’t need to go through a long, complicated process just to get one good piece of advice. A better approach is to ask two or three people for their input at most. If none of their suggestions feel right, take time to think for yourself and make your own decision. Everyone has to make their own choices in life, after all. If you do want to seek outside advice, look for a trustworthy adult who truly wants to support you—they’re far more likely to give you useful, well-thought-out guidance. I learned this the hard way when I had to plan a birthday party recently. I needed to pick outfits for all the guests and organize the whole event, but I was short on time and felt completely overwhelmed and confused about where to start. I reached out to friends, cousins, extended family, and even teachers, hoping someone could help. But instead of clarity, I ended up with a pile of conflicting ideas and couldn’t settle on any single plan.

What worked for me in the end was turning to my older cousin. We sat down and talked through every detail of the party, and she gave me a clear step-by-step plan. I was able to manage my time properly, pick out the right outfits, and get the entire party organized in just one week. Everything went smoothly, and that experience taught me how to make better choices for myself. If you can’t find a trusted family member to guide you, at least try to think through the problem on your own, or ask for help from someone you know is reliable. Avoid asking people you don’t know well, as they might not have your best interests at heart—some might even try to trick you, so you have to be careful. Overall, I’ve found that asking one trusted adult is far better than polling a huge group of people. When I first reached out to everyone I knew, I ended up more confused than before, and it felt like my whole world was spinning. It was my first time planning a big event, and I didn’t use my own judgment at all—it was a waste of time, and almost everything went wrong. That’s when I learned an important lesson: never make choices that your parents or other trusted adults would disapprove of. Another key way to make better decisions is to always listen to your parents and other adults in your life. Sometimes, the choices we make on our own seem great at first, but we realize later they’re not good for us at all. You might end up in trouble and have to deal with consequences you didn’t expect. That’s why it’s better to do what your parents tell you to do, rather than just following your own wants. It’s fine to listen to your heart sometimes, but that’s not always the right move. For me, the best way to make a good choice is to follow the guidance of parents and trusted adults.

There are a few core steps to making good decisions. First, use your own mind to weigh whether advice is helpful or harmful. Second, if you need outside input, ask an adult who is kind and honest. Most importantly, believe in yourself and in God. These are the most reliable ways to make smart choices. We should always have faith in both ourselves and our parents, because they will only ever suggest things that are good for us, no matter what. Whenever you’re unsure, remind yourself that your parents’ guidance comes from a place of care. Keep believing in yourself, too—if you stay positive and trust your abilities, things will work out. And remember to have faith in God, as he is always by your side and will help you through every situation. These are truly the best ways to make good choices in life.

Every person on Earth gets the same 24 hours in a single day. Have you ever stopped to think about how you spend that time? Do you actually check off tasks you set out to do, or do you end up lazing around? It’s common to start one task, then wish you were working on something else entirely at the same time.

As a student, I often have assignments and projects to finish. I used to promise myself I’d never slack off, but it’s not always easy. For instance, after school, I know I have a project due, but I also want to relax, do nothing, or eat dinner. My mind always feels torn. I have to ask myself what to tackle first. I’ve found that if I finish my project right away, I have the rest of the evening free to do whatever I want. That’s what makes a day feel successful to me.

I believe focusing on one task at a time helps me get more done. When I slack off, I waste time and can’t reach my goals. Every task has a process to follow. Some say you should never be idle for your whole life, but I don’t think that’s possible. Your life is yours to plan: you decide whether to do nothing or throw yourself into getting things done.

I’ve also found that working on tasks I enjoy helps me finish faster. Even when I’m idle, I can think through solutions to problems, or figure out how to reach my goals. When I hit a goal, I feel great about all the progress I’ve made. Life is about choosing: do you want to do more, or waste time being idle?

A number of people support Winston Churchill’s famous saying that success is about moving from one failure to the next without ever losing your excitement for what you do. They argue that failing teaches you valuable lessons, helps you get ready for future challenges, and gives you a clearer grasp of what works and what does not. On the other hand, many others disagree with this view. They do not see failure as something to value, since they believe that if they mess up once, they will naturally perform better the next time without needing to focus on the failure itself. It is also worth noting that no one is perfect: every person has both strengths and flaws, and this does not make anyone better or worse than the people around them.

Plenty of people see failure as a necessary experience to grow into a better version of themselves, but that does not mean they want to fail. Some believe that failing is an important part of life because it pushes them to learn new skills, and they put all their energy into becoming good, capable people. In fact, these same people try their very hardest to avoid failing at anything they do.

There is also another group of people who do not view failure as a negative setback at all. They argue that failing is just a normal part of life that helps you develop into a stronger person. For instance, if someone fails a class or does not get a passing grade, they will keep working at it and never quit. By learning from these experiences, they hold onto their enthusiasm and stay motivated to keep going.

It is clear that failing is not always the best route to achieving major success. If you want to succeed even after facing setbacks, you need to pay close attention to what went wrong, work on improving yourself, and put in maximum effort. When people make this kind of effort, the tasks they are working on will get better over time. Even so, plenty of people do go on to succeed after dealing with failures.

The truth is that failure is a normal, unavoidable part of life, and we need to make sense of our mistakes if we want to succeed. When we understand what went wrong, we learn how to do better next time, and we stop letting fear of failure hold us back. Letting go of worry about failing can actually give you even more enthusiasm to reach your goals.

Haveyou ever dealt with people who constantly pressure you to become someone you’re not?

There are plenty of people who argue that pushing others to change is positive, since they might care about the person but dislike certain parts of their personality. I completely disagree with this view. If someone truly cares about you, they will never try to force you to change. They met you knowing exactly who you were, flaws and all, and still chose to be with you and love you exactly as you are. If they start pushing you to be different, that proves they don’t actually accept you the way they claim to. In that case, it’s better to cut ties with them.

Never let anyone convince you to alter who you are. A person who really loves you will learn to embrace every part of you, including your imperfections. Your flaws are part of what makes you unique, and they matter just as much as your strengths.

Remember that the people who matter accepted you with all your quirks from the start. Stay true to yourself, and don’t let anyone mess with your self-esteem. It’s true that almost everyone will try to pressure you to change at some point, and some might even spread nasty rumors or say cruel things about you to wear you down. But you know your own worth, and you know exactly who you are.

If anyone ever tries to force you to become someone else, that’s a clear sign they don’t love you the way they say they do. Walking away from these people is the best choice, as staying around them can only hurt you in the long run.

That said, changing yourself is totally fine if *you* are the one who wants to do it. Just keep in mind that personal growth is a big decision, and it should only happen because you choose to, not because others are demanding it. After all, people who truly love you will never pressure you to change – they will treat you with kindness and respect exactly as you are.

Many people believe that influence is only useful for making money or building connections with wealthy, well-connected individuals who have ties to other countries and access to all kinds of benefits. They think these powerful contacts can help them find jobs or solve family problems, so they will never have to rely on anyone else for support.

Influence can also show up in your friendships. Sometimes, friends might pressure you into making terrible choices, like stealing or even hurting others. A lot of people seek out friends who are the most popular kids in school or the most well-known people in their neighborhood, even if those friends have bad habits. If you ever find yourself in this situation, stop and ask: why am I following their lead? Is this really the life I want? You have to be very careful, and never make big decisions in a hurry. Plenty of people end up in prison simply because they listened to what their friends told them to do.

I believe influence serves many different purposes in life. You can use it to earn money, build new friendships, and encourage others to do good instead of bad. A true friend will never stand by and watch you make a choice that could get you in trouble with the police, your school, or your parents. When people tell you someone is not a real friend, it’s usually because that person is not a good influence—real friends do things that keep you out of trouble, not actions that could send you to jail. Real friends will always be there for you when you need help.

Being influential means choosing to set a positive example for others, so they follow your lead and do good things too. The best way to be a positive influence is to do good deeds that make other people trust and respect you. Never think that acting out or doing bad things makes you more popular or influential, whether you’re in school or living in a small village. The only thing bad behavior will get you is a prison sentence or serious problems with the people closest to you. You have to make good choices in life, because if you don’t, you will face endless trouble.

Your influence affects everyone you meet, from your closest friends to strangers you’ve never spoken to before. If you want to be a good person, you may need to change the way you influence others. If you keep doing bad things, people will not want to be friends with you, because they don’t want to get in trouble or end up in jail for things like theft that they didn’t even want to do.

Some people believe that if you make bad decisions or do something very wrong, you are not a good person. Others say that holding this belief means you have never thought you could become a good person, no matter what.

You don’t have to change if you don’t want to, but keep in mind: if you want other people to trust you and respect your influence, you will need to adjust the way you act.

To me, there’s no difference between being the best influence and being a better influence. Either way, if you work to be a good person and change the way you influence others, you can achieve it.

The best kind of influence comes from doing good things for people who need help, or going out of your way to do something special for your friends and family.

Improving your influence is worth the effort, especially if people close to you or your family tell you that you need to change. One day, you will use your influence to get your dream job, or when you apply to offices for work. Many companies even say they value candidates who have a positive influence on colleagues from other countries.

If you have a history of bad behavior, you will never have a positive influence at work.

You will need a good influence in the future, whether that’s to earn more money or build relationships with people in your social circle.

You also need a positive influence in this life. You never know when you will need to use it, so keep doing good things, but never make bad decisions that could ruin your life.

To sum up, if you have a good influence on the people around you, never do anything bad that could land you in prison.

Many schools run programs that pair older students with younger ones to offer support. These programs step in when younger kids struggle with tasks, whether related to schoolwork or activities outside the classroom, and also assist students who need more support than their peers. This setup benefits everyone involved.

For older participants, these programs are valuable too. They often explain concepts they once found difficult, which strengthens their own understanding, and sometimes even learn new things while teaching. For younger students, the extra support pushes them to work harder and take on more challenges than they might face at home or in regular class. They can finish homework during the after-school program, so when they return to school, their work is done. This means fewer late assignments and better organization. At home, they can relax, play games, or go outside instead of stressing over work. These habits can even lead to better job opportunities later in life. I believe far more schools should offer programs like this, so more kids can access dedicated study time and better resources.

These programs create a cycle of support. If most schools adopted similar programs, younger students could get help from older peers, and those who finish their work early can assist even younger participants. Everyone gets the help they need, even if they usually do well in a subject like math but get stuck on harder homework. They might just need extra study time or to review past assignments. If that doesn’t work, older students step in to guide them through homework or projects. Peers can work together to finish faster, or choose to work alone if they prefer.

Once participants finish their homework—though most are still working on it—they have free time. Some use the computers, others go outside to play games. Often, half the group heads outdoors, and the other half stays inside, keeping the program fun instead of all homework and classwork. This keeps kids energized: after playing, they come back inside with fresh energy, instead of feeling bored or tired the whole time they’re at the after-school program.

I fully agree with Winston Churchill’s famous saying that success is made up of moving from one failure to the next without ever losing your enthusiasm. What really matters is not whether you fail, but that you keep your passion alive and at least make the effort to try—that is far more valuable than never taking a risk at all.

First of all, no one can ever know everything, but the most important thing is always making an effort. If you never try, you will never learn or grow. That said, failing without keeping your enthusiasm is a major red flag: it usually means you have stopped caring, or you are no longer interested in anything at all. Another clear sign of lost enthusiasm is wasting time. For example, if I feel like I am losing every time and have no passion or focus left, I will not put in the work to improve or become a winner. Instead, I will just waste my days—but if I hold onto my enthusiasm, I will make the most of my time to try to get better, and always work to improve.

Secondly, while many people want to become better versions of themselves, there are always those who refuse to put in the time to grow. I know for certain that some people prefer to stay exactly where they are: after all, if you want to be a winner, you have to try, experiment, and see what steps you can take to move forward. I plan to work hard to build a good future for my family, own my own home, and have the things I have always wanted. Letting yourself stay stuck in failure makes you look weak to others—people will assume you are not smart enough to do better, or that you are too comfortable with what little you have. Instead, you need to be ambitious if you want to gain more than your current lot in life.

Thirdly, if you do not want to stay trapped in failure, you have to seize every opportunity that comes your way. In this world, only those who use their minds wisely and avoid making big, careless mistakes get ahead. Of course, we are only human, and everyone makes mistakes sometimes—that is completely normal. What matters is that you fix your errors and work on improving yourself, while holding onto whatever inner drive keeps you motivated.

To conclude, in my opinion, there is nothing wrong with choosing to stay exactly where you are in life. However, you will never truly understand the meaning of life if you never take a risk and try something new. Everyone should make an effort to try at least once.

This well-known statement comes from Ralph Waldo Emerson, and it’s meant to guide people who are reflecting on their own lives: is it better to focus on individual work?

The core idea he shared is this: “To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.”

Understanding this message matters for everyone, especially people who want to make good life choices. You need to embrace this mindset early, before you run into issues with any organization you work for, no matter where you live. It also pushes you to think seriously about what you want for your future.

I fully agree with Emerson’s view, and I’d like to share why I think this is such a valuable accomplishment. First, you have to figure out what your life’s purpose is, and what you truly want to do with your time. You need to prepare properly to reach meaningful goals later, and get your life organized so you can succeed in whatever job or company you end up working for.

Working hard consistently makes you a better person to everyone around you, which is a clear sign you’re on the right track to success. Your family will feel proud of what you achieve, too. That’s why it’s so important to stay positive, act like a champion by putting in individual effort, and make smart choices for whatever organization you work for. You have to be careful here, though: always treat the people around you with respect, and they’ll be happy to work with you.

Putting in individual work is a huge help when it comes to achieving your goals. This is exactly why I agree with Emerson’s statement. He clearly focused on his own values and goals, and that helped him succeed. He made the right choices for himself, which is why he was able to write that famous quote in the first place.

Individual work is really just the collection of traits that make you unique, set you apart from everyone else, and define your personality. This is more important than you might think, because people in teams sometimes don’t put in full effort. They just work to get through each day, which isn’t a good way to live. You need to show up and work hard every single day to build a better future for yourself. If you don’t put in the effort, you won’t reach your goals. Keep going with the work you’re doing, because it will pay off later when you’re working with any organization.

The best accomplishments are the ones you earn through hard work. When you consistently put in effort, you’ll grow into a person who makes a real impact, both in your own life and in the wider world. Eventually, you’ll see the results of all your hard work. Believe in yourself—that’s one of the biggest signs that you’re on the right path.

The whole point is to stay true to who you are, even when the world pushes you to change. Your future is right in front of you, and putting in individual effort will bring happiness to both your future self and the people around you.

To wrap up, the key takeaway is to work hard for a better future, and make good choices when you interact with others—this will only help you in the long run. The point of Emerson’s statement is to focus on your own needs and goals so you can grow into the best version of yourself, and get your life organized. That means making smart choices, not letting bad experiences drag you down. If you hit a rough patch, never stop working hard. Based on my own experiences, I fully agree with Emerson’s idea that someone who has become mastered will never make progress.

First, when people fall into this mastered state, it blocks them from growing in whatever they are trying to achieve. For instance, imagine you work as a store manager, and you notice that sales of all your products are dropping, and your business is not doing well. Naturally, you might feel useless, and think you should switch to selling different products or close the store. But if you let yourself become mastered, you will feel awful about yourself, and start to think you are not good enough to keep your job. You get so focused on seeing your work fail, instead of looking for ways to improve it.

Second, being mastered often happens when you are convinced you are right about something, and a friend challenges you, pointing out that you are wrong about your approach. Once you realize your friend was right and you made a mistake, you might try to fix things, but then you slip into that mastered state. That makes you feel like you have no chance to try again. Most people feel too discouraged to attempt something they have already mastered poorly. For example, if a teenager takes a test at school and gets a low score, they will feel so upset that they refuse to retake the test, because they have already let themselves become mastered by that failure.

Third, many people are scared to try again at something they care about, worrying that the result will be exactly the same as the first time. But if you do try again, you will have more experience to draw on, and you can work hard to avoid repeating the mistakes you made before. You will be more careful, because you know what went wrong last time. We can all try things more than once—the key is to believe in yourself. You will see that you can grow, no matter how hard things get, or how many times you feel upset. You have to stay positive, even if you feel scared after having been mastered before.

To sum up, you should never give up on something you have tried, no matter how many times you fail, or how many times you feel like you have become mastered. You always have another chance to start over. Trust that you are capable of doing it—that is all you need to begin again.

I fully agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s famous quote on individuality: "To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment." I believe this holds true because of three key reasons: achieving meaningful success, staying true to who you are, and taking full control of your own life.

First, genuine success benefits society as a whole. We need people who follow their own passions to become philanthropists working to reduce global poverty, or inventors creating tools we now rely on every day, like cars, the internet, and computers. When people refuse to conform to others’ expectations, they drive human progress, building safer, healthier environments where everyone can live long, fulfilling lives.

Second, staying authentic is a major achievement in itself. When you are yourself, you become exactly the person you want to be, rather than a version of yourself shaped by others’ demands. You build honest relationships with the people around you, because you show them your true self instead of putting on a fake version of who you are. Most importantly, you live a life that feels meaningful, rather than following a path the world has chosen for you.

Third, taking charge of your own life is incredibly valuable. You get to make your own choices, from small daily decisions to big plans for your future. Being the one to make these calls makes your life feel more fulfilling, and it often leads to better overall health too.

Some people argue that individuality is pointless, or that it is easier to let others tell you what to do. But I believe that building your own success, staying true to yourself, and controlling your own life are essential not just for individual happiness, but for the progress of all humanity. Every person should have the right to decide who they want to become and what goals they want to pursue.

All these factors add up to a truly great personal achievement. Think of life as a book: every person has their own unique story to tell. Choosing to be yourself, rather than accepting the pre-written life the world tries to force on you, is always the greatest accomplishment. Too many people are conditioned to follow paths laid out for them, but breaking free of that to live as your true self is what really matters.

I strongly believe that cultivating a positive attitude is essential for building a better life. When you approach life with optimism, you are far more likely to achieve the goals you set for yourself.

To build this positive mindset, I follow a few simple steps:
- Make time for fun, interesting activities
- Seek out new experiences to try
- Talk to trusted friends when I need support

Not everyone agrees that living positively is worthwhile, though. I think some people reject this mindset because they feel they have nothing to look forward to, like a stable future. As I mentioned before, a positive attitude is vital for success. If you don’t make an effort to stay positive, you will never improve your life and will stay stuck in the same routine. For example, learning new things every day is much easier when you have an optimistic outlook, which is why I stand by this belief. Staying positive also opens up more opportunities for me to succeed.

To maintain a positive lifestyle, I like to relax, read books, listen to music, go for walks, or chat with supportive friends. These activities help me push aside worries and negative experiences. Being prompt means acting quickly to finish tasks on time or even early. While it helps you get everything done ahead of schedule, rushing without planning can lead to problems, so it’s important to think carefully about your priorities and stay cautious when working fast.

To sum up, I strongly agree that being prompt and maintaining a positive attitude are both valuable. I like being able to finish tasks efficiently, and both habits help me work toward a better life for myself.
