I always brainstorm topic ideas before writing anything down. My first draft is handwritten, and I edit it around five times, adding extra words whenever the content feels too short. Once I’m happy with the handwritten version, I type it up on my computer. Then I rewrite it again to check all spelling is correct. Next, I review each sentence to fix any remaining spelling errors, looking up unknown words in a dictionary right away. I check the paper to make sure it makes sense to my reader, then do another edit to add extra sentences or better word choices, using the dictionary for new terms. Finally, I do a last full revision to confirm everything is right.

Many schools have special programs for new students who have just enrolled. These students take a test first so teachers can assess their current English level and place them in suitable classes to learn more of the language. Students with limited English join these dedicated classes to improve their skills. After regular school hours end, we offer summer school sessions where students can keep practicing English. Without summer school, learners might forget much of what they have learned, even though teachers are still available to help both older and younger students. Program availability varies between schools: some have different classes, some run unique programs, and others share the same courses, though not all do.

I think schools that offer remote learning options are a fantastic choice for many people, for several key reasons.

Many want to complete their education but can’t attend in-person classes. Some lack time because they need to work, pay bills, and handle daily tasks. Others leave school to support their families: they care for younger siblings, spend time with loved ones, or work to bring money into their household.

Remote classes work best for students continuing their education after high school, whether at university or other programs. They can work to cover course costs, since many programs are too expensive for parents to pay alone. This lets them keep up with classes while earning money to fund their studies and build their future.

Studying from home is also more relaxed and focused. Without campus distractions, learners can study calmly, worry less, and balance coursework with work, free time, and other tasks as they prepare for a better future.

Overall, distance learning is the top choice for many. It lets people juggle work, childcare, personal time, and family time all at once. For anyone wanting to finish high school or university studies, remote classes are the most practical option.

Many people claim that keeping a positive mindset is the most important factor for success in life. I partially agree with this view: optimism helps in many cases, but it is not a universal rule.

For one, a cheerful outlook can definitely lead to success. Take basketball legend Michael Jordan as an example. He was cut from his high school varsity team early in his career, but instead of giving up, he stayed upbeat, practiced tirelessly, and became one of the greatest athletes of all time. His positive attitude and hard work laid the foundation for his huge success.

Another clear example is rapper DaBaby. Early in his life, many people told him he would never amount to anything. However, he stayed humble and positive, refusing to let criticism get him down. Today, he is one of the top rappers in the music industry, with multiple gold and platinum albums, millions of followers, and sold-out shows worldwide. His success is directly tied to his refusal to lose hope.

That said, I also disagree that positivity is always the key to success. Soldiers deployed in active war zones cannot afford a carefree, sunny mindset — they need to stay alert to enemies and ready for danger at all times. In this high-stakes situation, a relentlessly positive attitude could even be a disadvantage, as it might make them less cautious of risks.

Some students ignore their teachers during lessons because they place little value on their education. While many teachers encourage pupils to focus on their studies, they may not mind if students get distracted by their phones. On the other hand, plenty of students are eager to learn and never let their devices interfere with their work.

There are schools that allow cell phone use in classrooms, often because teachers are busy with other tasks, or they simply tell students they can use their phones if they wish. In some US states, by contrast, phones are banned from classrooms entirely, as schools prioritize academic focus over device use. Even so, a few teachers there experiment with phones to gain more classroom experience, though they still try to limitstudent phone use. Overall, policies vary widely between different schools.

In other countries, phone use in class is strictly prohibited. Students caught using a phone may have their parents contacted, or even be expelled from school. To succeed academically, students must follow their teachers' instructions, which also helps them grasp lesson material more effectively.

Some schools do not enforce strict phone rules, as long as students stay focused on their studies. If pupils want to use their phones, they are told to do so only after class ends. This is because while some students use phones to chat on Snapchat or Facebook, others use them to look up information related to core subjects they already have some knowledge of, to deepen their learning.

Many students turn to their phones in class simply because they have no engaging activities to do. Schools need to provide more hands-on learning experiences to keep students occupied. When lessons are well-structured and interesting, students will no longer feel the need to use their phones, as their classmates also benefit from a focused learning environment.

Students need more meaningful learning opportunities at school overall. If schools fail to provide these, more students will end up using their phones during class time. While some students are responsible enough to use their phones for learning, not every pupil can handle that level of freedom.

People should focus on earning achievements to build their self-esteem. Working toward clear goals helps them develop more skills, put in more effort, and feel a genuine sense of purpose when they reach a target. Some argue that praise is better for boosting the confidence needed to learn, but confidence built only on compliments often does more harm than good. Students who get praised without earning real accomplishments may grow lazy, assuming they do not need to work hard to succeed.

There are clear reasons why achievement is far more valuable for self-esteem than empty praise.

First, focusing on achievement pushes students to work harder than praise alone ever could. For example, imagine a student who puts in hours of effort on a task. If their teacher only offers nice words instead of acknowledging the actual progress they have made, the student might lose motivation or feel upset. To keep making progress, students need to see real results from their hard work, not just praise.

That is not to say praise is a bad thing. It can be encouraging when paired with real success. But when it comes to building lasting self-esteem, achievement should always come first.

Take a school art project as an example. If one student finishes their work successfully, simply praising another student who did not put in the effort makes no sense. Recognizing actual achievement gives students a proud record of their success that stays with them throughout their school years.

Lastly, achieving goals makes students far happier than receiving praise. A good grade, like an A or B, or the satisfaction of completing a tough task feels much more meaningful than empty compliments. True self-esteem grows from these real wins, not from being told you are good without proof.

These are the three key reasons why self-esteem comes from achievement.

In China, we don't hold the same belief as Ralph Waldo Emerson. I understand that Ralph Waldo Emerson believed he grew as a person by pushing past skills he had already perfected. In my view, everyone is unique, so not all people will grow simply by tackling tasks that go beyond what they already know well. Moving past an activity you have already mastered does not automatically mean you are growing. I disagree with Emerson’s claim for three key reasons: first, seeking out and learning new skills can help people grow. Second, even tiny but important details can spark growth. Third, many other major life events also help people mature. I do not agree with what Ralph Waldo Emerson wrote.

First, learning new things is a clear path to growth, even if those new skills are not necessarily harder than what you already know. New things we learn are often outside our full control, full of surprises we cannot plan for. When students pick up new information, their knowledge base expands, and that process helps them mature. My mother is a perfect example of this. When she first moved to the United States, she did not speak a single word of English. She spent three years studying the language, and now she can hold basic conversations with others. No one can argue that she has not grown during this time—she mastered a completely new language she had never encountered before. Her experience taught me that growth does not only come from pushing past what you have already mastered; picking up entirely new skills works just as well.

Second, even small, seemingly unimportant details can lead to major growth. Think of a science experiment: a tiny error in measurement can destroy all the work put into the project. For students studying science, making that small mistake might lead to harsh criticism from their professors. But few people realize that these small, frustrating moments can also change how a person grows. I believe these small setbacks are actually big opportunities for scientists to mature. They have the power to control whether such mistakes happen again in the future. This example shows that small issues can grow into bigger problems that affect your whole life, and learning to handle them is a key part of growing up.

Third, many ordinary life events can help people grow, not just academic or work-related challenges. When you enter the workforce, you quickly realize how different the real world is from school. You learn that hard work is not the only way to get ahead—there are many different paths to reach your goals. Understanding this is a sign that you have truly become an adult. Getting married is another major milestone: your wedding day is one of the happiest times of your life, and it pushes you to grow again as you take on new responsibilities. Then, when you have a child, you finally understand what true responsibility means. That sense of duty is exactly what we call growth. There are so many parts of life—your job, your spouse, your children, and countless other experiences—that help people reach full maturity.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once wrote, "Unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow." This idea might hold true for Emerson or some other people, but I do not agree with it. Everyone is different, and we all have our own unique ways to grow, not just the single path Emerson described. People can expand their knowledge by studying new things. They can learn valuable lessons from small mistakes they make. They can also grow by navigating the challenges of society. Here in China, there are countless experiences that push people to grow every day.

To achieve great things, we need to stay consistently active in whatever we take on. The more effort we put into different tasks, the more likely we are to reach the goals we’ve set for ourselves and keep moving forward in life.

Take Thomas Jefferson as an example: he achieved a huge amount in his lifetime, most notably drafting the Declaration of Independence. He never wasted time lounging around or hanging out idly with his friends when there was work to be done.

Most of us set personal goals at the start of every year. The following year, we work to tick those goals off our list. The process of chasing these targets means we are always occupied with some task or another—this cycle never ends, because humans are naturally driven to keep working. Plenty of people fritter away their time, though, and never end up finishing the goals they set. Deep down, everyone has a personal motivation, a spark in their heart that pushes them to keep going and make something of their life.

Think about how much the world has changed over the years: we have new smartphones, updated sneaker designs, better TVs, and countless other innovations. Behind every single one of these ideas is a person who worked tirelessly to make improvements. Our world runs on constant activity—each generation builds on the last, achieving new things year after year.

When we take on tasks, we do so with a clear purpose. It is incredible how persistent people can be—we rarely give up entirely, and we always have some project or task on the go. If others see you sitting idle with nothing to do, that time feels wasted, both for you and for the people around you.

This is how society functions: we go to school to learn, then move on to college, then find a career path that suits us. Every step of that journey requires active effort to reach your goals, improve your quality of life, gain more knowledge, and grow as a person. There is no room to stop when you are chasing what you want.

We only make progress when we stay consistently busy. Throughout life, there will always be people pushing you to do better—sometimes you will feel like doing absolutely nothing, but even small tasks matter. For example, imagine you have summer break: you stay home all day playing video games, eating snacks, and never lifting a finger to work. You leave the dishwasher full of dirty dishes, never clean the house, and ignore your responsibilities. When your parents get home and see you lounging around, they will probably be upset. They might tell you to put down the controller, start helping with housework, wash the dishes, and even get a part-time job to earn some money. That is the moment you realize you need to start taking action to accomplish the goals your parents set for you, instead of wasting your time at home doing nothing.

So, do we achieve more when we are always active? The answer is a clear yes. Never stop taking on tasks, because even when you don’t notice it, every day you are accomplishing something new.

When it comes to navigating life, we all face a choice: should we make our own choices, or rely on experts and authority figures who have more experience? In my view, starting out on your own, even with no prior experience, is far better. You get to shape your own journey, follow your own plans, and no one interferes with your goals. Making your own decisions and setting your own rules is key. After all, if you have someone more experienced watching over you, they will constantly correct you and get in your way. While some people prefer following others’ lead, I believe being independent is the better path. You get to build your life on your own terms, just like how no one tells you how to run your own family. Other people’s advice might even be wrong, while your own choices could be right. Being alone lets you create the life you want, using your own decisions and rules, not someone else’s.

First, being independent helps you grow through your own mistakes. When you make your own choices, even if one leads to an error, you gain valuable experience from that slip-up. Every mistake teaches you a lesson, making you more responsible over time. These experiences make you stronger in whatever you do, and that sense of growth feels rewarding. As you learn from your own errors, you become more accountable for your actions. Other people will notice this resilience, and they will start to see your potential. They will trust that you can succeed in the future, because you built your skills on your own, not by leaning on someone else’s guidance. When you are alone, you rise based on your own decisions, not someone else’s.

Another key point is that you should set your own rules. When you create guidelines that work for you, no one can argue with them if they want to be part of your life. But if you spend time with someone more experienced, you will be forced to follow their rules, which is rarely what you want. When you stick to your own rules, you know exactly what outcome to expect. If you follow someone else’s rules, you are always in the dark about what might happen next. That is why making your own decisions and rules is better: you understand the value of what you are doing, and you can predict the results. Following your own rules makes you a stronger, smarter person, instead of just doing what someone else tells you.

Finally, the last major reason to stay independent is that no one will interfere with your work. You take full control of every task, rather than leaving decisions in someone else’s hands. No one will hover over you or nag you to change your plans. When you handle everything yourself, you become an expert in your job, your studies, or any project you take on. You are the one in charge of your choices, not relying on someone else’s judgment. If you use someone else’s ideas, they will constantly correct your work, pushing you to do things their way instead of yours. This is frustrating, because they will try to force you down a path you do not want to take, making every effort to get you to follow their preferred route. You should stick to your own path, so you can gain your own experience and set your own rules without interference.

To sum up, everyone should make their own decisions, rather than relying on more experienced people or companies to guide them. You should start from nothing, and over time, you will gain experience from the mistakes you make along the way. As you build more experience, you grow stronger and expand your knowledge. Others will see your progress and believe you can reach your goals. It is also vital to create your own rules, and be thoughtful about the guidelines you set. Do not follow rules made by others; when you make your own, you can predict whether things will go well or poorly. Following someone else’s rules leaves you guessing, so setting your own is the only way to stay true to yourself and become an expert. On top of that, being independent means no one interferes with your work. You are in charge, no one tells you what to do, and as others see you succeeding on your own, you will grow even more in your field. Eventually, you may even guide others who want to follow your path. All things considered, the best choice is to be independent, not lean on others who will make decisions for you. When you rely on someone else’s experience, you miss out on building your own. No one will bother you when you are on your own, so take that first step and start from zero. You will be glad you did.

Winston Churchill once said that success is moving from one failure to another without ever losing your enthusiasm. I completely agree with this statement. When you work toward any goal, you will have wins sometimes and setbacks other times, but the most important thing is to never quit. Looking back at my own life, I’ve started plenty of projects that I haven’t finished yet, but I haven’t given up on them. I know I will complete all of them soon. For example, many people start out with lots of motivation: they win a few times, hit one failure, and immediately quit. If you truly love something, you have to keep chasing it, or you will never achieve it.

Failure is a word no one likes to hear. Many students get upset when they fail a test or a class, because they can’t accept not being the best – they only care about winning. The same is true for work: if you want to get a raise or a promotion, you have to show up on time, work hard, and improve a little bit every single day. Soccer is a great example of this. To succeed in soccer, you have to master new skills and practice all the time. Winning doesn’t happen by accident: you have to put in consistent effort and do things right every time. We all hate failing – I hate it too, and I often feel like it’s just a waste of time. I’ve failed so many times, but I never give up, because I know I need to finish what I started to eventually succeed.

Enthusiasm is the real key to reaching your dreams. If you don’t have passion for what you’re doing, you’ll never get good at it. You might fail more than once, but you have to focus on the reward that’s waiting for you, stay positive, and remind yourself that you will be successful. Take my own experience with college as an example. I wanted to go to college, but I started working first and began earning a good salary. Later, when I thought about going back to school, I looked at all the hard work and assignments required, and I almost gave up. I had lost the enthusiasm I felt at first. Why? Because I got distracted by making money and other things, and I didn’t feel like I was making progress toward success.

That is why I agree with the former British Prime Minister Winston Churchill. To get what you want in life, you have to fight for it. Never give up when faced with new challenges. You will fail sometimes, but you have to pick yourself up and keep going. That’s how you grow, get better, and keep a positive enthusiasm for life. Everyone deserves to be successful, so never lose your enthusiasm – it is the most important key to success.

The ancient storyteller Aesop once shared a wise thought: no kind deed, no matter how tiny, is ever pointless. To me, this also applies to how we handle hard times, like losing a loved one. Even when you are furious or deep in sadness, there is still room to find glimmers of hope. If a family member passes away, it is right to feel grief, but you can also take comfort knowing they are in a better place, free from pain or suffering.

Another way to take this quote is as a reminder to stay true to yourself. Do not let other people drag you down or tell you that you are wrong. If you believe something is right, go after it, and prove any doubters wrong—you are capable of far more than you might think. Of course, you might make mistakes along the way, but that is okay. Learn from those errors and try again.

Finally, this saying reminds us to cherish small joys, especially in childhood. Kids have carefree fun, but as you grow older, you will take on big responsibilities: finding a job, buying a home, getting a car, and handling other tasks. Adult life is not as lighthearted, so make the most of little things and have fun while you still can.

If I had to choose one job to pursue, I would pick working as a soldier. I have two main reasons for this choice: the role offers strong pay, and it lets me protect the people of my country.

First, the pay for soldiers is far better than many other jobs, which would help me support my family. I once heard a story about a boy named Generic_Name, who was in the tenth grade and originally dreamed of becoming a nurse. His parents disapproved, pointing out that nursing does not pay enough to lift the family out of financial struggle. Generic_Name also wanted to earn enough to give his loved ones a comfortable life, but he felt torn when his parents shut down his nursing plan. He shared his frustration with a close friend at school the next day. His friend admitted that while nursing is a noble job, it would not meet Generic_Name’s financial needs or help his family. “Maybe your parents are right,” his friend told him. “Nursing is a good job, but it won’t give you or your parents the financial security you need.” Generic_Name asked, “But isn’t nursing a good job too?” His friend replied, “It is, but it’s just not the right fit for your situation.” Generic_Name thought over his friend’s words for a long time, then decided to switch paths and train to be a soldier. Though he was hesitant at first, he worked hard in his training program, then went to college to complete his studies. He graduated at the top of his class, then applied for a role as a soldier. When he got the job, his first big purchase was a new house for his family. He never struggled with money again, and was even able to support his parents financially. His family was incredibly proud of him, and he felt like all his dreams had come true. This story shows how being a soldier can solve money problems for both the worker and their loved ones.

Beyond the pay, I want to be a soldier because I want to protect the people of my country. There is another story about a girl named Generic_Name that shows this. She lived with her mother and father, and had no siblings. Her father was a soldier, and she grew up admiring his work, but in their community, women were not allowed to fight in wars. One day, a messenger came to their home to tell Generic_Name’s father that war had broken out in their town, and the army needed him to report for duty immediately. But Generic_Name’s father was very sick, and could not go. The family’s only child was Generic_Name, a girl, so there was no other man in the house who could take his place. Generic_Name’s father wanted to go anyway, but she stopped him—she knew he would die if he went to fight, and she also could not bear the thought of her town being destroyed. Even though she was a girl, she decided to go fight in his place. On the way to the army camp, she disguised herself as a boy, cutting her hair and wearing men’s clothes, knowing the general would send her home immediately if he learned her true gender. When she arrived, she trained hard alongside the other soldiers, and was ready when the fighting started. The general ordered them to prepare for battle, planning to shoot the enemies as soon as they arrived. But the enemy had planned a sneak attack, and when the two sides met, almost all of the soldiers in Generic_Name’s unit were killed, leaving only her alive. She fought fiercely, taking down every enemy soldier until the battle was won. She was so exhausted after the fight that she collapsed and fell asleep right on the battlefield. While she slept, her fake hair fell off, revealing her true gender. When the other soldiers found her, they were overjoyed to have won the battle, but shocked to see she was a girl. “A girl! She’s a girl!” one of them shouted. When the general arrived, he was furious and wanted to have her executed for lying about her identity. But then he remembered that she had single-handedly won the first battle, saving the army from defeat. He decided to let her go home with strict orders to never return to the camp.

Later, the enemies surrounded the remaining soldiers and launched a new attack. News of the attack spread quickly, and the villagers were terrified because there was no one left to protect them. Generic_Name did not want the general to die, so she came up with a plan. She snuck into the enemy camp and killed most of the invaders, then approached their captain. “Your highness, I know the person who wants to kill you,” she lied. “He said he is not afraid of you, and he is waiting for you outside the camp.” The captain asked, “Do you know where that person is now?” Generic_Name replied, “Yes, he said he’s waiting for you.” “Take me there,” the captain ordered, and she led him out of the camp. But when they arrived, there was no one there. “Where is the person?” the captain asked. “I am the person,” Generic_Name said. At first, the captain laughed at her, thinking she was joking. But when they started fighting, she killed him, saving the town from the attack. After that, the army officially accepted her as a soldier, and everyone in the community respected her. She proved that women are just as capable as men in combat roles.

These two stories sum up why I want to work as a soldier: the job pays well enough to support my family, and it lets me defend the people in my country. The first Generic_Name thought nursing was the right path for him, but switching to soldier work eliminated his money struggles and let him give his parents a better life. The second Generic_Name faced discrimination because she was a girl, but she proved that women are strong enough to serve as soldiers just as well as men. Some people believe only men can work in the military, but that is completely wrong—anyone, regardless of gender, can take on this role if they are willing to work hard. If you are a woman who wants to be a soldier, do not let anyone stop you. This job is open to all of us, not just a small group of people.

Working in a group has clear advantages over working by yourself. When you work with others, you can share knowledge to solve problems more effectively, while working alone means you only have your own ideas to rely on. I have three key reasons why group work is better, and three reasons why I avoid working solo. For group work, my reasons are that we tackle tasks together, get more support from teammates, and feel more at ease. When working alone, I have to back up all my ideas by myself, no one can help if I get stuck, and I often feel more frustrated if my work takes too long or my ideas are not good enough. I believe group work helps students more because we can support one another.

My first reason for preferring group work is that we work together, which makes it easier to finish tasks on time. We all share information with the team, and everyone contributes their own knowledge. This also makes me feel more motivated, as I get energy from working with others.

My second reason is that group work offers more support. We can help each other out, which is a key skill to learn. I like group work more for this reason: if someone in the team does not know the answer to a problem, the rest of us can step in to help them figure it out.

My final reason for choosing group work is that it feels less stressful. You do not get as frustrated, because other team members can help you if you get confused by a problem. They can offer support to work through tricky questions, so you never feel stuck on your own.

These are my three reasons for preferring group work over working alone. I find solo work far more frustrating, and you get no support from others. Group work is easier because we can check each other’s ideas and split tasks — one person can handle one part of the work while another does a different section, so everyone has less to do. This makes the whole process smoother.

First impressions are incredibly tough to shift, as the initial image I project to those around me sticks in their minds. The way I interact with others during that first meeting often dictates how they will treat me going forward, and most people are very reluctant to revise their initial judgment of me.

First encounters carry weight because they form the baseline for how everyone around me will view me. Once someone has met me once, that snapshot becomes their impression of me. If that first impression is negative, that is how they will remember me every time they cross my path later, even if it does not reflect my personality. For example, if I was having a terrible day and acted short-tempered during a first meeting, people will label me as a grumpy person, even if I am usually cheerful and upbeat.

The way others perceive me is largely tied to the first impression I made on them. If I gave off a bad vibe initially but later try to act friendly and kind, they are unlikely to trust my changed behavior. They will hold onto their original negative view of me, assuming I am putting on an act or being dishonest about my true character.

How I treat people during that first interaction also determines how they will treat me in return. This two-way dynamic makes it even harder to shift their opinion of me later, as they will keep mirroring the attitude I showed them initially.

It is worth noting that while people rarely change their minds about first impressions easily, it is not impossible. If I put in consistent effort and act with good intentions, the other person may eventually revise their view of me. In some cases, I do not even need to make a deliberate attempt to fix a bad first impression: my actions over time can shift how others see me. This works both ways, too—I could turn a poor first impression into a good one over time, or ruin an initial impression with consistent bad behavior.

To sum up, first impressions are very difficult to reverse. The initial image I project shapes how others perceive me, dictates how they treat me in return, and sticks in their minds for a long time. However, with patience and consistent effort, it is still possible to change what people think of me.

Many students who live a long distance from their school buildings choose to take their courses entirely from home. While this setup might seem convenient at first, it can seriously harm a student’s education and even their future prospects, since not every learner enrolled in remote classes will actually finish all their required work. I strongly believe attending classes from home is a poor choice, as it is far too easy for students to get distracted, fall behind on assignments, and end up with failing grades.

Remote learning can be especially challenging for people who tend to lose focus easily. I once had a friend named Generic_Name, who was enrolled in an online math course that she had to pass to graduate. One day, I stopped by her house around 6 p.m. after my own school day ended, and she was sitting at her desk with her laptop open to her online class portal. But she wasn’t actually working on her math assignments at all. Even though her class page was pulled up, she was completely fixated on a TV show playing in the background: Beauty and the Beast, which she loved. She’d completely stopped doing her schoolwork to watch it. If she had just turned off the television, she wouldn’t have been distracted, and she would have been able to keep up with her class and pass easily.

Another issue is that when students take classes from home, there is no one there to remind them to stay on track with their work. Many end up forgetting to submit assignments, leaving them with incomplete coursework. This year, I am taking an online class myself, and I sometimes completely forget that I have assignments due. Just last week, I received a low grade because I never completed a vocabulary assignment that was required. If I had set a daily alarm to remind me to check my school portal and work on my tasks, I would have gotten a much better score.

Some people argue that learning from home is a good idea because students can work on their own schedule, at any time that suits them. However, others point out that it often leads to poor grades. I have noticed that several classmates taking online courses do not bother to read all the instructions provided by their teachers. They rush through assignments without checking the guidelines, which always hurts their final grades. Earning bad grades can even put you at risk of failing the entire school year, but if students put in consistent effort, they can still do well.

While online classes may seem like a good option for some students, they can often end up hurting their education in the long run. Many students enrolled in remote courses are falling behind because they do not have enough support, while others are struggling simply because they refuse to do the work. If schools offered after-school help sessions specifically for online learners, it would make a huge difference for students who need extra support to succeed. This would help them feel more comfortable while working on their assignments, and teachers could also regularly check in to make sure students are on track to pass their classes.

Many people argue that a positive attitude is the most important factor for success in life. I fully agree with this view, and I can back up my stance with both academic research and my own personal experiences that prove a positive mindset is truly the key to achieving one’s goals.

Each morning when we wake up, we should focus on the tasks we need to complete for the day, rather than being lazy or aimless. Having a clear plan and a positive mindset keeps us from feeling bored, and gives us the energy to keep going. For instance, if a student knows they have a test in their next class, they can plan to review their study guide and do extra practice that night — this preparation will help them earn a great grade on the exam. Another key point is that students who want to get into good colleges can volunteer in their free time or study for the SAT to boost their scores, while also taking AP classes to raise their GPA. For example, spending weekends volunteering at a local hospital or library lets students gain real-world social experience that helps with college applications, and setting aside time to prep for the SAT and finish homework on time keeps them on track.

About two years ago, I had a friend who told me she wanted to own a bookstore that also served coffee. Today, she has achieved that goal. During her four years of college, she worked a part-time job for half the day every single day. She saved money, gained work experience, and even learned how to create beautiful latte art on coffee cups. She also kept notes on which books customers liked to read most, because she always knew exactly what she wanted to achieve.

To sum up, I strongly believe that a positive attitude is the most important key to success in life. We need to figure out what kind of life we want to build, and with the right mindset, we can all look forward to a brighter future.

Starting an after-school homework club is an effective way to improve student achievement at my school. Many students struggle with their assignments and need extra support to grasp what they are learning in class. When teachers stay after class to work one-on-one with these students, they can clear up confusion before tests, which helps them earn better grades. After all, students who review material through homework with teacher guidance are far more prepared for exams. However, some students refuse to stay after school even when a teacher offers to help. This is frustrating for teachers, who often rearrange their schedules to make time for these sessions, only to have no one show up.

Teachers already give up personal time to support students, hoping to help them get good marks on their report cards. Many care deeply about students submitting homework on time, and some even grant extensions when students ask. But when students waste these opportunities and still don’t complete work, some teachers stop offering extra time altogether. They tell students their final grade will come down to whether they finish assignments or not. A dedicated homework club would solve this issue: only staff assigned to the club would stay after school, rather than random teachers having to sacrifice their free time or stay late to prepare next day’s lessons. Sadly, some students don’t appreciate these efforts at all—they even throw their homework in the trash, unconcerned with how hard teachers work to give them a quality education.

Students who understand the material and finish assignments quickly could volunteer to help peers in the homework club. In theory, this peer support is helpful, but in practice, when teachers let students work together, they often end up playing or chatting instead of focusing on work. Interestingly, this changes if the students don’t know each other well—they are more likely to stay on task and actually help. Even so, some students dislike getting help from classmates. They find that peers just hand over answers instead of explaining concepts the way a teacher would. When a teacher asks these students to explain their work, they can’t, which makes it obvious they copied someone else’s answers.

Test scores and overall achievement would improve significantly if the club is launched. Many students skip homework because they don’t understand the material or simply forget about it. Doing work in the club after school removes these barriers, making assignments feel less difficult. Some students claim they have no homework for certain subjects, but when they fail to turn work in, they tell teachers they had too much to do and forgot it at home—even though they never even attempted the assignment. Even when teachers try to offer extra support, these students refuse to try, preferring to accept a bad grade rather than do the work.

Other students prefer to finish homework early to avoid staying after school. They use free class time to work on assignments, asking teachers or classmates for help if they get stuck. This way, they can relax at home without worrying about unfinished work. For students who don’t want to work with peers, the club also offers the option to get one-on-one help from a teacher. Many teachers support peer tutoring in the club, as they find that students explain concepts to each other in ways that help them ask questions and better understand what they learned in class.

A lot of students would improve their grades if teachers called their parents to require them to stay after school for the club. Many young people go home and play instead of doing work, then lie to their parents when asked if they have homework. If teachers reach out to families to explain that a student is failing a class because of unfinished assignments, and that the student doesn’t seem to care about turning work in, it pushes students to take the club seriously. Offering small rewards to students who stay and finish work on time would also boost motivation, as they can see their grades improving and feel proud of their progress.

Homework clubs at other schools already show that regular assignment practice helps students perform well on tests. If you don’t do homework, you will almost certainly struggle when exam time comes, since you haven’t reviewed the material. Some schools don’t offer these clubs because they assume all students understand their work—no one asks for help, and teachers never see unfinished assignments turned in. In these cases, teachers think students just don’t want to do work, or believe them when they lie about leaving homework at home, even when students get good grades without doing the assignments. Student volunteers at these schools often give up their time to help peers who are struggling, but rarely get thanked for their efforts.

Ralph Emerson once wrote that staying true to who you really are is a struggle for many adults, but for teenagers, this challenge is even greater. From childhood, most people grow up knowing exactly what path their life is expected to follow, which makes breaking away to be yourself feel almost impossible.

Teenagers who grow up with a family that pays attention to their daily lives and supports their choices are fortunate, since not everyone has that kind of stable foundation. For teens whose families show no interest in their well-being, the struggles they face are more intense than those of their peers with supportive homes. These young people are forced to make a choice early on: either work hard to become a good person, make their family proud, and prove they can succeed even without help, or fall into harmful habits that could lead to jail time. When a teen lacks family support, they take any available work to put money in their pocket and put food on the table for their loved ones. To me, being yourself means looking out for your own future and your family’s well-being, and making sure your younger siblings get chances you never had. Most people make this choice during their teenage years. It is one of the toughest decisions anyone can make, as it requires leaving your past behind entirely and pushing yourself to work hard enough to never slide back into old, difficult circumstances.

Those who made this choice when they were young know exactly how that situation feels. They learn how to stay true to themselves, and figure out what it really means to act like a responsible, grounded person. The world is not kind to people who lack strength — only those with strong wills manage to get by, while those who are weak often fail. That is why being yourself requires a tough, steady mind above all else.

For students who are too sick to attend school in person, especially those staying in hospitals, online classes are an incredible help. Kids with serious conditions like cancer or other chronic illnesses can keep up with their schoolwork without putting other students at risk of getting sick.

Some people argue that even sick students should come to school no matter what. But they’re wrong. These students don’t hate school—they’re not just trying to skip class for fun. Their bodies are too weak to handle the commute or being around crowds, and they get sick easily. While schools do allow sick students to take online classes, there’s a catch: families have to pay extra for them. That’s really unfair. These students already can’t join sports teams or participate in most school activities, and now their parents have to cover the full cost of their classes too. It’s a lot for families to handle, and students should be grateful to their parents for covering these costs.

Do schools really have the power to force a sick student to attend in person?

I still remember when I was 5 years old, I caught a nasty cold and my parents told me I had to go to school anyway. I started crying and refused to leave the house. My grandpa heard me and came over to talk. He told me to stop crying, eat my breakfast, and get ready for school. When I asked why I had to go when I felt so terrible, he shared a story from his own childhood. When he was a student, there were no online classes at all. Even though he faced huge challenges, he worked incredibly hard and eventually became a doctor. After hearing that, I dried my tears and went to school, thinking about the example my grandpa had set for me.

THINK ABOUT

It has been a long time since then, and I’m 18 now. I’m so grateful for what my grandpa taught me. He showed me that education is hard to access if you stay home all the time—online classes won’t give you the same value in the end. It doesn’t matter if you take online classes or in-person ones, but you have to put in the work. Sometimes you’ll want to stay home, hang out with friends, or take the easy way out, but if you use online classes as an excuse to slack off and put off your work, you’ll regret it later. You have to think about what really matters in the end.

There are two paths you can take: one leads to a bright future, the other to a harder life. If you care about your family, who love and support you, you’ll want to make them proud. Work hard, go to college, and build a happy life with the people you love.

I agree with the proposed half-day school schedule. Teachers are already organizing engaging, fun activities for students to enjoy during these shorter days, which makes the plan even more appealing.

The main benefit of shorter hours is that students get to go home earlier. This gives them extra time to finish any classwork or homework they didn’t complete during the school day. Some teachers also support this change, as they believe students can use the extra time at home to rest and spend more time studying.

Of course, not everyone is on board. Some people disagree with the plan, worrying that letting students leave early will lead to them skipping their schoolwork. But I think it’s good to mix up the daily routine instead of doing the exact same thing every day. Half days add welcome variety to students’ schedules.

Another key advantage is that shorter school days give school staff more time to prepare for the next day’s lessons. When schools have extra time to get ready, students get a better quality of education, which helps them become more productive later in life. Some people prefer schools to stick to full days, but I don’t think keeping school hours exactly the same all the time is a good idea.

In the end, a large number of people support the half-day plan, and I count myself among them.

I agree with Emerson’s view that the skills and knowledge we have already mastered are a big advantage in life. It is always easier to complete tasks when we are familiar with the work, after all. But if we never step outside of what we already know, we will never discover what else we are capable of. To grow, we have to keep improving ourselves and set new goals, instead of staying stuck in the same place doing the same things every day. Nothing is impossible, no matter where you start in life.

Many people struggle to believe in their own abilities, but even those of us who were born into poverty can achieve what we want. If we work at it over time, we can reach the dreams we have always had. There are so many opportunities in the world, and you will see your life change for the better if you pick a new goal and refuse to give up.

Sticking to what we know feels safe and comfortable, as I see in my own work. I am employed as a busboy, where I help servers as part of a close-knit team. The job is straightforward and familiar, but I want to become a server myself. My managers have not allowed me to try the role yet, but moving into that position is my next goal. It would let me grow professionally and earn more money to support myself.

We should all look for ways to create new opportunities and try new things, using the skills we have to keep growing. Do not be afraid to step outside your comfort zone if you want to improve your life. I have no interest in staying in the same position doing the same tasks forever, because I see no progress that way. Your life could change completely in just a week, but you have to stay positive and keep trying. There is nothing bad that can come from giving new opportunities a chance, so do not give up.

Does technology have a more positive or negative impact on our daily lives? In my view, technology brings more harm than good to people’s lives, mainly because most of us struggle to use it in moderation. Nowadays, far too many people forget how fulfilling life can be without screens. We are perfectly capable of enjoying ourselves without any devices: we can play outdoors with friends, visit libraries, or spend time surrounded by nature. There is a common debate about how much screen time children should have. Some argue that kids need strict limits on their use of computers and cell phones. Others claim that teenagers benefit from having no restrictions, as it lets them learn more. Personally, I believe teenagers need clear boundaries for what they do on their phones, and parents should regularly check what their children are doing online.

Some people still argue that leaving teenagers unrestricted online is good for their future learning. However, others point out that teens often struggle to finish tasks when they do not have face-to-face contact with others. I believe talking to people in person is far better: it helps you get to know someone properly and strengthens your relationship with them. Meeting strangers online is risky, as not everyone has good intentions. Many parents assume their kids only play games when they are online, but this is not always true. Whether it is chatting online or playing silent video games, I think there shouldbe limits on these activities until you are certain you know the other person well.

Another major issue is online shopping. Many people buy lots of items from websites without knowing the sellers personally, which is very dangerous. Sellers on websites may not actually have the products they advertise, or they might only care about taking your money. If you do buy something online, always make sure the website is secure first. Relying on online shopping has become a problem because it stops people from going out and spending time with their families. Since sites like Amazon and eBay became popular, most people get all their needs delivered instead of going to physical stores. Criminals take advantage of this trend by creating fake websites to scam unaware shoppers.

To get children away from screens, parents should encourage them to have fun outdoors with friends. Having online friends through video games or social media is not healthy for kids. You should always get to know someone in real life before playing or talking to them online. Unfortunately, some people trick children into doing harmful things, so this caution is especially important for young people.

For this reason, I believe technology should not be allowed for children at all. If parents do choose to give their child a cell phone or computer, there must always be strict limits on how and when they can use it.

Technology also makes it hard for people to complete tasks without human interaction, which I see as another negative effect on our lives. Many people get scammed because they use so many untrustworthy websites. No website is completely safe, so everyone needs to set their own limits and be careful online. Children are especially at risk, as they are losing their childhoods to screen time. Parents must step up and enforce strict limits on their kids’ technology use to protect them.

Many schools now offer distance learning as an option, letting students attend classes from home via online platforms or video conferencing. However, I believe this is not a good idea for most learners.

First, home environments are full of distractions that make it hard for students to focus. Televisions, video games, and cell phones often pull their attention away from lessons. Reports show 80% of students who take distance learning classes do not benefit from them because of these interruptions. Another 20% avoid distance learning entirely, saying it is too difficult to manage. Even 5% of learners report that cell phones alone stop them from concentrating at home. Many students do not complete assignments, and some even copy work directly from the internet instead of doing their own tasks. Cheating is also common: some learners copy answers during tests or use online sources to finish projects without putting in their own effort.

Socially, distance learning is also lacking. Students who learn from home often have no friends, since they do not work in groups or interact with peers. This lack of social connection adds to their distraction, as they miss the structure of learning with others.

There are a few small benefits to distance learning that some students mention. For example, they do not need to shower in the morning or wake up early for class. A small number of people also prefer learning from home to avoid bullying based on skin color. However, most students find in-person school much more fun, and say they are less distracted there than at home.

Cost is another issue. Video conferencing classes still require payment, even for students who have part-time jobs and already pay for their education. Many people have mixed opinions about this: some say online learning is a great idea, others think it is terrible. At our school, students often talk about school fees, but most agree that going to campus is easier. They say they make more friends in person, and understand lessons better because teachers can explain questions right away, or help with work immediately when they get stuck.

In-person school also offers resources that distance learning cannot match. There is a library, physical materials like paper and notebooks, and meals including breakfast and lunch. Students can take all types of classes, from art and geography to music. While some people find learning from home easier to avoid bullying, the downsides far outweigh these small benefits.

Overall, distance learning via online tools or video calls is not a good choice for most students. The distractions, cheating, and lack of social connection make it less effective than attending school in person.

Should art, music, and drama classes be required core subjects or electives? I believe they should definitely be offered as electives. Right now, many students already take these courses as electives to make sure they stay on track to graduate on time. Most students enjoy drama, art, and music classes way more than mandatory core subjects, which are already required to earn a diploma. Electives are meant to be fun, after all, while core classes focus on the essential requirements for graduation. Making these creative classes electives also gives students a chance to try new things, pick up new skills, and figure out what they might be talented at.

Some people argue that art, music, or drama should be required core classes, but I disagree. These creative subjects are less important than core classes like math, English, or science, which teach essential skills students need for their future. That said, taking one of these classes as an elective is still really enjoyable. It lets you experience something totally new, outside of your usual coursework. You also get to meet people you might not cross paths with in your regular core classes, which makes the experience even better. That’s exactly why they should stay as electives, not become required core subjects.

If you try something you’ve attempted before that didn’t work out, don’t let that get you down. The more times you make an effort, the stronger you’ll become, and the more control you’ll gain over your own life. Stay calm, believe in yourself, and you’ll find that more opportunities open up for you. Putting yourself out there to try new things (or retry old ones) shows you’re capable of far more than you might think. Ultimately, it all comes down to you: if there’s something you’re truly passionate about, go after it. Don’t let other people’s opinions hold you back – no one else can live your life for you.

I disagree with what author Ralph Waldo Emerson wrote on this topic. Just because you’ve tried something before and failed, or even messed up every time you attempted it, does not mean your life is over, or that you can’t keep growing. That idea is completely wrong. If you’re committed to a goal you care about, you might face setbacks or failure many times, but you shouldn’t let that wear you down. Keep pushing until you reach the dream you’ve been working toward.

My father is a singer who has always been incredibly determined, and he knows exactly what he wants. Years ago, he took part in a major music project. He’s a very talented vocalist, but on the day of the final performance, he lost his voice completely. Even so, he gave it his absolute best, and ended up winning the project anyway. After that win, many people reached out to work with him on all kinds of large, diverse projects. Now he’s a well-known star, and he’s grown so much as both an artist and a person. This proves that trying again leads to huge growth, as long as you’re certain of what you want and truly enjoy what you do. Never give up – I’ve lived this lesson myself, too. When I first moved to the United States, I didn’t speak a single word of English. It was incredibly hard to get by here without knowing the language – all my homework and school projects felt impossible to complete. But I never gave up, and I’m still growing every day. I keep trying new things, and I’m still making steady progress.

There are plenty of common sayings about this: some people claim that if you’ve already mastered a skill, you’re guaranteed a bright future. Others argue the opposite – that spending so much time chasing one specific goal is a waste of your life, because you’re letting that one thing take over everything else that matters.

Lots of people try many different things, fail, and eventually give up on their original goals. But others keep pushing, giving their absolute best until they finally get what they want. Always do your best and never quit. If your family or friends tell you that you won’t grow any more, or that you’ll never amount to anything, don’t listen to them. You’re stronger than you even realize – just keep going. Even if you’re already an expert at the thing you love most, you can still grow a huge amount, because you have a chance to show others exactly who you are and what you’re capable of. Keep your faith in your goal. I do not agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s view – I think he is completely wrong. Just keep working hard and never stop, because everything is up to you.

I believe working in groups is the most effective approach for students. You may wonder why I hold this view. For one, group work is a great way to learn. Take me as an example: I am the kind of student who enjoys hearing what others think about a topic. Listening to classmates’ perspectives gives everyone involved a clearer idea of how to tackle a project or assignment. When students get the opportunity to share their thoughts, they grow more confident and feel less afraid to speak up.

Of course, plenty of students prefer working by themselves. They often say this is better because no one interrupts them with endless questions. Most solo workers already have a clear topic and a solid plan in place before they start. For instance, students who work alone can move at their own speed, which gives them a better chance of meeting deadlines on time.

Working in a group allows everyone to split the workload into smaller, manageable sections. For example, one person can handle the research, another can design the project layout, and a third can write a specific section of the assignment. Breaking the project into parts lets students pick the tasks they find easiest or already have experience with, which makes the whole process smoother.

Group projects also give students the chance to meet new people. Sometimes you don’t get to pick your teammates at all—professors may assign you to work with people you’ve never spoken to before. Collaborating with unfamiliar peers can introduce you to new working and writing methods. For instance, I once worked with a classmate who created a T-chart to list the positives and negatives of a topic side by side, which helped them decide which side to argue in their section. Seeing this approach gave me a new tool to use in my own work.

Group work also speeds up the entire process. As mentioned earlier, dividing tasks means everyone can focus fully on their assigned part, which gets the work done much faster. If you finish your section early, you can volunteer to help a teammate who is struggling. For example, a student working alone might take far longer to complete a project because they have no one to share the load. If you have spare time, you can offer to help them with a part they find difficult, which benefits everyone.

To sum up, working in groups teaches students to listen to and value others’ ideas, and it is the best way to learn to collaborate as a single team. That said, some people argue that working alone is the better choice, as it teaches students to make decisions independently and write their own papers without relying on others for help.

I don’t believe modern technology harms people in any major way. In fact, as tech advances more and more every single day, it makes starting and managing daily life far easier for everyone. It’s also great for staying in touch with other people, whether that’s chatting with friends or playing online games together. There are so many practical uses for it: you can work remotely, shop online instead of going to physical stores, and even teach others who are less familiar with how tech works. These days, knowing how to use technology is basically a requirement. For example, many job applications have to be submitted online, so you need basic tech skills to even apply for work. A clear example of how useful it is? We can now use digital maps to find any location instantly, something that was impossible not that long ago.

The biggest reason technology is so valuable is that it lets you get done whatever you need to do. But if you have no idea how to use basic tech tools, that quickly becomes a problem, since you won’t know how to handle everyday tasks. That’s why it’s worth practicing how to use different devices and programs. For most jobs, you need to know how to operate a computer, and even using a smartphone like an iPhone requires learning how its features work. You’ll also often find friends or family asking you for tech advice, so you need to understand how to use these tools properly. Most importantly, always use technology for positive purposes, never for harmful ones. Just because you know how to do something with tech doesn’t mean you should say yes to every request, especially if it feels wrong.

Of course, technology has some downsides too. For example, many children now know far more about tech than they should for their age, and this affects their lives in negative ways. They can get almost anything they want just by using tech skills, which means they don’t learn to work hard at different, non-tech tasks. While you can build a career or future around tech-related projects, you should always talk to experts before making big decisions in this field. Don’t let constant tech use ‘contaminate’ how you think or act. Always remind yourself that what you’re doing with technology is worthwhile and positive.

Always listen to your own inner voice when deciding if a certain use of technology is good or bad, and never ignore that instinct.

Modern technology lets you do countless things, but you have to set limits for yourself and stay aware of what you’re doing with it. Too many people only use tech for harmful or pointless activities, and they don’t even pay attention to how their actions affect others. We all need to understand that we shouldn’t use technology for negative purposes, and take a clear stance on what we will and won’t do with it. Think carefully about what you’re creating or doing online. For instance, tech now lets us track where someone is located, and you can do almost anything with just a phone or computer: play games, chat with friends while gaming, or handle all your banking tasks online, like depositing checks without ever going to a bank branch. All of these uses show exactly why technology is so important in our lives today.

When pleasant events happen, many people naturally feel cheerful. Instead of dwelling on negative feelings, they focus only on staying in a good mood.

Others might not pay much attention to their current mood, choosing instead to do fun activities to lift their spirits. Ideally, everyone should stay happy and avoid feeling sad, angry, or down. Bad moods often come from small issues, like waking up on the wrong side of the bed, or a parent scolding them for something they didn't even do. Even though many people struggle with constant sadness, a lot still maintain a positive attitude. It is also common for people to get angry over tiny, unimportant things, which often leaves others wondering why they are so upset.

When someone is feeling down or needs support, we should try to cheer them up, especially those who are bullied. Everyone should be kind to others, and only share personal thoughts with people they truly trust, not with fake friends. If you face any problems, it is always a good idea to ask a teacher for help. No one should ever feel sad in this world, since God created it so that people can be happy, smile, and treat each other with kindness. We should never engage in bad behavior, and always aim to stay in a good mood.

Don't let others dictate how you live your life. Be yourself, believe in your abilities, and never give up. If your friends tell you that you are not capable of achieving things, they are not real friends—you should distance yourself from them. Do not let unkind words get you down. Always try your best, and surround yourself with genuine people.

At school, focus on doing well and avoid being in a bad mood. If you act upset in class, people might assume it is the teacher’s fault, or that you dislike school and find it boring.

Why is it important for people to make their own choices? I believe everyone should take charge of their own decisions, rather than letting others pick for them. After all, every person has to make their own choices in life, and doing so is incredibly useful. When you decide for yourself, you understand your own needs far better than anyone else does, so you always know the right steps to take.

This is your life to live, so you should be the one making choices about how to lead it. When you make your own decisions, you gain far more freedom to live exactly the way you want. Everyone, without exception, should make their own choices. We all need to do this because it brings more freedom, helps us figure out the best path forward, and can even make day-to-day life feel simpler. Other people’s decisions are often hard for us to relate to, since we don’t know their full circumstances. That’s why I think our own choices are always better than following what someone else would pick for us.

Choosing for yourself gives you the freedom to do whatever you want, both in your daily routine and for your long-term future. Our own choices are better than what others would decide for us, because when you make your own calls, you can always stick to what feels right for you. I really do think making our own choices is the best approach. We get to pick the things we actually enjoy doing in life. When we decide for ourselves, life becomes much smoother and less stressful.

Other people’s decisions are often totally different from what we would pick, or we might even dislike their choices entirely. If we try to follow someone else’s decisions instead of our own, we’re likely to run into a lot of struggles. Making your own decisions really can make life feel easier overall. Everyone has different wants and needs, so what someone else chooses might not work for us at all. That’s exactly why I think every single person should have the right to make their own choices. Deciding for yourself leads to a happier, more fulfilling life in the long run, because you’re living on your own terms. Since this is your one life to live, you should be the one picking the path you take.

At the end of the day, our own choices and decisions are always better than what other people would pick for us. I believe people should keep making their own decisions, because everyone has to make their own calls in life. It is truly helpful to decide for yourself, as you will know better what to do. This is our own life, so we should be the ones making decisions about it. Other people’s choices can be hard for some to understand, and if we don’t like each other’s decisions, we will both have a difficult time.

I think collaborating with a team is far more useful than working solo, because when you have a reliable crew, you can get far more work done, put effort into tasks, wrap up projects efficiently, and even earn more money collectively as a team.

As for working alone, I’m much less confident in that approach. Solo work can be really tough, since you’re responsible for every single task, and it’s hard to know if you’ll even finish on time unless the job is very small. For larger projects, you might end up spending a full day or even two just to get it done.

I have firsthand experience with group work. Once, my team had to process 6 pallets, and we got down to just 2 remaining. We finished all the pallets so quickly that we thought we’d be able to leave early, but we all pitched in to wrap up the final tasks together.

Working alone was a totally different story, and it was way harder. I tried to finish just one pallet on my own, but I couldn’t manage it. There was so much stuff packed into a single pallet, and to be honest, I was still new to that department. That’s exactly when they sent someone to help me out.

All in all, working as part of a group is far more helpful than working solo. There are plenty of benefits to both approaches, but if I had to pick the better one, I’d go with group work every time. The only exception is if the task is small, and you’re certain you can handle it on your own.

While some people argue that students’ self-esteem should be built through praise—claiming this helps them perform well on exams or pass their courses—I believe true self-confidence grows from real achievement instead. This is because students put genuine effort into their work, make sure they have the energy to keep going, and consistently work hard to produce their best possible results.

First, students put real effort into their studies. If they miss a class, they often stay after school to catch up on missed assignments with their teachers. Even when they hope for praise after doing something well, they always study first to earn good grades, rather than expecting compliments without working for them. They might even dislike doing homework during school breaks.

Second, students take steps to stay energized for their schoolwork. They eat breakfast every morning and bring snacks from their house to keep their energy up during the day. They know that being self-confident is essential for learning, so they ask their teachers for help when they struggle, and their teachers are always happy to assist them. They also make sure to organize all the papers and handouts their teachers give them.

Finally, students work consistently to produce their best work. They study at home after school, finish all their homework, and practice extra exercises during breaks or once they’ve completed their assigned tasks. Many also visit the library to borrow books related to their classes, to make sure they have all the knowledge they need to pass their courses.

To conclude, while some claim praise is the best way to build students’ self-esteem, especially when they have exams or need to pass a class, this is not true. Genuine self-esteem comes from achievement, as students put in hard work, stay energized for their studies, and constantly strive to do their best. It is this real accomplishment, not empty compliments, that deserves praise and helps students build lasting confidence.

I strongly agree with the view that staying true to who you are is key. Being yourself is a personal choice that requires you to stay consistent with your own personality. This way, you can feel proud of the choices you make in life. If you want to grow into a kind, good person in the future, you must treat others with respect.

First, being yourself is a deeply personal act. If you pretend to be someone you are not, you will never become a truly good person. At the same time, you need to have a kind personality and show respect to others if you want to stay true to yourself. Anyone who lacks these traits does not have a strong, positive personality.

Another important point is that even when other people act unkindly or fail to show respect, you still need to stay confident in who you are. You should aim to be a positive, supportive member of your community. This helps ensure that the people around you are comfortable with you being your true self.

We interact with other people constantly in our daily lives, which is why we need to stay confident. This helps us choose to be kind, honest, and respectful to everyone around us. Being generous also helps us grow into the good people we hope to become in the future.

Finally, it is worth noting that some people in a community may not respect others for being themselves. For example, if you achieve something meaningful, others might try to find faults in you. That is why you need to stay confident and generous. You must remind yourself never to compare your life to someone else’s, because doing so will stop you from being a good person.

In conclusion, these are the main reasons why staying true to yourself matters. You must remain consistent with your own personality, so you can feel grateful for the actions you take in life. If you want to become a kind, good person in the future, you need to treat everyone with respect.

When people turn to others for advice, the most common topics are usually related to sports or schoolwork. For example, many ask for guidance on how to improve at a sport, or how to tackle their homework assignments. Often, this kind of advice works a lot like a teacher’s instruction: someone walks you through the steps needed to finish a task correctly.

One very common situation where people seek advice is when they are new to a school. If a new student asks many people for help, it is always good to offer support.

I fully agree with this statement. These three concepts accurately capture how we express our deepest emotions. The three key ideas are: first, anxiety; second, suppressed feelings; third, a lack of self-belief.

1. Be anxious. Nearly everyone in the world has countless thoughts racing through their minds: how to finish work tasks, handle daily chores, and solve personal problems. This constant mental load creates huge pressure, much like physical force leaves a mark on a surface. That pressure leaves a clear impression of their true emotions, built up from past experiences. Many choose to hide these feelings because they are worried about being judged, so they keep their struggles to themselves. This habit of bottling up anxiety stops them from making positive changes to their lives.

2. Suppressed feelings. Many people struggle to show what they are going through. They feel disconnected from their own wants and needs, and often feel confused about what they should do with their lives. They are terrified to open up to others, fearing their emotions will be dismissed. On top of that, they believe that any mistake they make is permanent, and that things can never be set right again.

3. Lack of self-belief. Some people do not trust or value themselves, so they depend on others to handle their responsibilities, often pretending to feel a certain way to fit in. They frequently ask other people to do even simple tasks for them, such as sending someone else to fetch something they need because they feel too ashamed to do it themselves. This reliance on others leaves them unable to handle their own duties.

The truth is, nothing is impossible. We are capable of achieving anything we set our minds to, and we can choose the path that feels right for us. Life is always changing: our friends, our daily routines, our emotions, even every passing second. Never feel shy about admitting what you truly want or need. You will never be perfect if you never make mistakes—those mistakes are exactly what help you grow and improve in the future. If you choose the right path, you can become the best version of yourself, secure a good place in life, and live happily without pretending to feel things you don’t.
